title: CLAUDE.md
text: forestsearch R package (CRAN-targeted, lifecycle: experimental) implementing Forest Search methodology Leon et al. (2024, Statistics Medicine, doi:10.1002/sim.10163). performs exploratory post-hoc subgroup identification clinical trials: enumerates candidate subgroups baseline factors, screens effect threshold indicative harm/benefit, selects subgroup “maximally consistent harm” via repeated split-sample evaluation, produces bias-corrected treatment-effect estimates infinitesimal-jackknife confidence intervals. Originally survival-(Cox HR), package extended current branch (feature/glm-extension) GLM outcomes: binary (/RR/RD), continuous (mean difference), count/rate (IRR via Poisson/quasi-Poisson/negative-binomial). Much code branches outcome_type ("survival"/"binary"/"continuous"/"count") effect_measure.

title: CLAUDE.md
text: pipeline four-stage flow; stage separate exported entry point consumes previous stage’s result object. 1. Search — forestsearch() (R/forestsearch_main.R, largest file ~2700 lines; helpers forestsearch_helpers.R). Constructs candidate binary factors (LASSO via glmnet, GRF via grf, quartile splits), enumerates one- two-factor subgroup combinations meeting min-sample/event criteria, screens effect threshold, runs split-sample consistency select estimated subgroup. Returns forestsearch S3 object. Data preparation (factor processing, dummy encoding, candidate construction) lives get_fsdata.R + get_FSdata_helpers.R. Subgroup enumeration/scoring subgroup_search.R. 2. Consistency — subgroup.consistency() (subgroup_consistency_main.R + subgroup_consistency_helpers.R). Repeated random 50/50 splits (default R=400), optionally two-stage sequential early stopping. select_best_subgroup() applies selection rule ("hr", "maxSG", "minSG", "hrMaxSG", "hrMinSG"). 3. Bootstrap bias correction — forestsearch_bootstrap_dofuture() (bootstrap_dofuture_main.R, bootstrap_analysis_dofuture.R, bootstrap_calculations_helpers.R, summaries bootstrap_summaries_helpers.R / summarize_bootstrap_results.R). Re-runs full search inside bootstrap replicate, applies two-source bias correction log-effect scale, computes IJ variance. Parallelised via doFuture/future/foreach. 4. Cross-validation — forestsearch_Kfold() / forestsearch_tenfold() (forestsearch_cross_validation.R, summarize_cv_results.R). N-fold (leave-one-) repeated K-fold CV stability; cv_metrics_tables() reports sensCV/ppvCV/exact-match. Effect estimation backends. Cox-based estimation: Cox_estimation_helpers.R, cox_ahr_cde_wrapper.R, cox_spline_fit.R. GLM-based estimation (extension): glm_effect_estimators.R, glm_effect_profile.R, glm_spline_fit.R, generate_glm_dgm.R, grf_subg_harm_glm.R, calibrate_glm_interaction.R. make_effect_estimator() dispatches outcome type. GRF layer. grf_main.R, grf_helpers.R, grf_args.R, grf_subgroup_labels.R wrap Generalized Random Forests candidate/policy-tree subgroup discovery. DINA. dina*.R family (dina.R, dina_subgroup.R, dina_bagged.R, dina_subgroup_bootstrap.R, dina_subgroup_refit.R) distinct “difference--nested-…” bagged-subgroup method S3 classes print/summary/plot methods. Simulation & operating characteristics. generate_aft_dgm_*.R (flexible AFT data-generating mechanism), setup_gbsg_dgm.R/sim_aft_gbsg.R (GBSG-based DGM reproducing paper sims), simulate_from_dgm.R, run_simulation_analysis.R, oc_analyses.R, simulation_tables.R, truefind_asymptotic*.R. MRCT regional-consistency sims mrct_simulation.R. Visualization & tables. plot_subgroup_results_forestplot.R (main forest plot), plot_sg_weighted_km.R, plot_km_band_forestsearch.R, plot_spline_treatment_effect.R, gg_forest.R, render_forestplot.R; gt-based tables create_summary_table.R, format_subgroup_summary_tables.R, summary_utility_functions.R. S3 dispatch primary polymorphism mechanism — print/summary/plot/coef/confint/predict methods across forestsearch, dina*, fs_forestplot, fs_kfold, fs_tenfold, fpr_calibration, etc. forestsearch_methods.R fs_debias_gate_methods.R hold method definitions. Check NAMESPACE (generated) full S3 method registry.

title: CLAUDE.md
text: File organization: one major exported function per R/<name>.R file, named function. Single-use helpers live file, prefixed . marked @noRd. Helpers shared across functions get *_helpers.R file. Global variables: utils::globalVariables() declarations consolidated R/globals.R (suppress NSE NOTEs data.table/ggplot2/dplyr). scatter globalVariables() calls elsewhere — add new NSE column names globals.R. Dependency weightedsurv GitHub-package (Remotes: larry-leon/weightedsurv), installed automatically source, CRAN. Parallelism: entry points take parallel_args = list(plan = "multisession", workers = N). Default worker count floor(0.80 * physical_cores), auto-capped 2 R CMD check (_R_CHECK_LIMIT_CORES_) CRAN compliance — see .default_parallel_workers(). Argument capture: forestsearch() mirrors resolved formals args_call_all via .sync_args_call_all() bootstrap replicates can reconstruct exact call; adding formal must survive bootstrap, add sync list. DGM wrappers around generate_aft_dgm_flex() take base_args named list (...) override utils::modifyList(base_args, list(...)), never c(). CRAN hygiene: use pkg::fn() matching @importFrom; ASCII R source (use >= ≥, ≥ strings); wrap slow examples \dontrun{}/\donttest{}.

title: CLAUDE.md
text: reflect standing instructions author keeps quarto/claude code notes/CLAUDE.md: Scope discipline: modify explicitly requested. opportunistically fix, refactor, restyle unrelated code. Flag side issues separately end turn rather silently fixing . Source truth: file path cited, recent version shared conversation. editing file, re-read edits rather trusting stale view. Don’t commit push without explicit approval; propose commit messages instead. Never rewrite history (rebase/amend/reset --hard) without asking. Don’t bump DESCRIPTION version/deps, run install.packages() nontrivial chains, delete files without asking first. Present tradeoffs short numbered list clear recommendation. Honest disagreement welcome; explain reasoning substantive statistical claims rather asserting. Statistical vocabulary (used precisely throughout vignettes/code): distinguish marginal Cox HR (dgm$hazard_ratios$overall, attenuated non-collapsibility — never call “true HR”), average hazard ratio (AHR), individual/patient-level HR. Calibration targets AHR default. Verification per task task’s acceptance tests, nothing else. Write tests/testthat/, run devtools::load_all() + testthat::test_file(), gate files green. run full devtools::test() suite, run R CMD check rcmdcheck form, part task. full suite CRAN check run Larry explicitly asks — typically install release, never otherwise. Two check surfaces exist case. certification surface bare R CMD check ---cran (via rcmdcheck::rcmdcheck(args = "---cran")) — builds PDF manual, catches LaTeX-unsafe Rd content surfaces miss. devtools::check() certification: manual = FALSE default passes ---manual, skipping PDF manual build, can report 0 errors | 0 warnings | 0 notes tree certification surface flags. either run, pandoc PATH non-interactive Rscript session machine, export RSTUDIO_PANDOC=/usr/lib/rstudio/resources/app/bin/quarto/bin/tools/x86_64 (put PATH) R CMD build fails “Pandoc required build R Markdown vignettes available”.

title: Binary and continuous outcomes: the ACTG 175 analyses
text: ACTG 175 randomized HIV-infected adults four antiretroviral regimens. analyses compare zidovudine plus didanosine (ZDV + ddI, arm 1) didanosine alone (ddI, arm 3): 1,083 patients, every one week-20 CD4 count. Twelve baseline covariates enter every search: age, days prior antiretroviral therapy, weight, Karnofsky score, baseline CD4 CD8 counts, six binary indicators — haemophilia, homosexual activity, history injecting drug use, race, sex symptomatic status. trial whole combination leaves fewer patients without CD4 improvement spares 28 cells per mm³ CD4 decline. Every bound read two effects.
code: actg <- subset(speff2trial::ACTG175, arms %in% c(1L, 3L)) actg$id    <- seq_len(nrow(actg)) actg$treat <- as.integer(actg$arms == 1L)           # 1 = ZDV + ddI, 0 = ddI stopifnot(nrow(actg) == 1083, !anyNA(actg$cd420))   # every patient has a week-20 CD4 count  cont_vars   <- c("age", "preanti", "wtkg", "karnof", "cd40", "cd80") bin_vars    <- c("hemo", "homo", "drugs", "race", "gender", "symptom") confounders <- c(cont_vars, bin_vars)  # Binary endpoint: 1 = no CD4 improvement at week 20, the adverse outcome. # The binary covariates stay numeric 0/1; forest search treats them as categorical. df_bin <- actg df_bin$y_binary_neg <- as.integer(!(df_bin$cd420 > df_bin$cd40)) for (v in bin_vars) df_bin[[v]] <- as.numeric(df_bin[[v]])  # Continuous endpoint: the CD4 decline from baseline to week 20, positive = worse. # The binary covariates are factors, as in the applied analysis this one follows. df_cont <- actg df_cont$y_decline <- df_cont$cd40 - df_cont$cd420 for (v in bin_vars) df_cont[[v]] <- as.factor(df_cont[[v]])  # The whole-trial effects, with Wald 95% intervals wald <- function(fit, back = identity) {   b <- coef(fit)[["treat"]]; se <- sqrt(vcov(fit)["treat", "treat"])   back(b + c(0, -1, 1) * qnorm(0.975) * se) } whole_or <- wald(glm(y_binary_neg ~ treat, family = binomial, data = df_bin), exp) whole_md <- wald(lm(y_decline ~ treat, data = df_cont)) c(patients = nrow(actg), ZDV_ddI = sum(actg$treat == 1), ddI = sum(actg$treat == 0),   no_improvement = sum(df_bin$y_binary_neg)) #>       patients        ZDV_ddI            ddI no_improvement #>           1083            522            561            430 cat(sprintf("Whole trial: odds ratio of no improvement %.3f (%.3f, %.3f)\n",             whole_or[1], whole_or[2], whole_or[3]),     sprintf("             mean difference in CD4 decline %.1f (%.1f, %.1f) cells per mm3\n",             whole_md[1], whole_md[2], whole_md[3]), sep = "") #> Whole trial: odds ratio of no improvement 0.665 (0.520, 0.850) #>              mean difference in CD4 decline -27.6 (-43.1, -12.1) cells per mm3

The naive median over events only — # median(time[event == 1]) — is biased downward in the presence of # censoring, since the KM curve accounts for the at-risk set at each # event time.  If the KM curve does not cross 0.5 the median is # returned as NA (event time "not reached"). km_overall <- survfit(Surv(time_months, status) ~ 1, data = gbsg) km_median  <- summary(km_overall)$table[["median"]]  cat("N =", nrow(gbsg), "  Events:", sum(gbsg$status),     sprintf("(%.0f%%)", 100 * mean(gbsg$status)), "

") (After building dgm_uniform, exp(dgm_uniform$model_params$mu) should be similar.) .t_dgm_start <- Sys.time()  # ── All arguments to generate_aft_dgm_flex() except k_treat ─────────────── # k_treat is the calibration parameter; everything else is fixed up front. base_args_uniform <- list(   # ── Required: source data & outcome ─────────────────────────────────────   data                = gbsg,   continuous_vars     = c("age", "size", "nodes", "pgr", "er"),   factor_vars         = c("meno", "grade"),   outcome_var         = "time_months",   event_var           = "status",   # ── Treatment ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────   treatment_var       = "hormon",   draw_treatment      = FALSE,                                  # default   # ── HTE specification — uniform treatment effect, no embedded subgroup ──   model               = "null",                                 # uniform HR throughout   subgroup_vars       = NULL,                                   # default — no embedded HTE   subgroup_cuts       = NULL,                                   # default   k_inter             = 1,                                      # default (irrelevant under "null")   spline_spec         = NULL,                                   # default   set_beta_spec       = list(set_var = NULL, beta_var = NULL),  # default   # ── Censoring model (independent of treatment effect) ───────────────────   continuous_vars_cens = NULL,                                  # default → inherit   factor_vars_cens     = NULL,                                  # default → inherit   select_censoring     = TRUE,                                  # default — AIC select   cens_type            = "weibull",                             # default   cens_params          = list(),                                # default   cens_intercept_only  = FALSE,                                 # default   # ── Super population & misc ─────────────────────────────────────────────   n_super             = 5000,   standardize         = FALSE,                                  # default   seed                = 99,   verbose             = FALSE )  # ── Step 1: calibrate k_treat so that the AHR is exactly 0.70 ───────────── # We calibrate to the AHR (average hazard ratio over the super-population), # not the marginal Cox HR, because the simulation analyses below fit a Cox # model stratified by `grade` — and under Cox non-collapsibility the # marginal Cox HR on fully-observed potential outcomes is attenuated toward # 1 relative to both the AHR and the stratified Cox HR.  Calibrating to the # AHR makes the simulation median HR track 0.70 closely; calibrating to the # marginal Cox HR (`use_ahr = FALSE`, the default) would pull the simulation # median below 0.70.  See `?calibrate_k_treat` for both options. k_treat_uniform <- calibrate_k_treat(   target_hr_overall = 0.70,   base_args         = base_args_uniform,   k_treat_range     = c(-5, 5),   tol               = 1e-6,   use_ahr           = TRUE,   verbose           = TRUE )  # ── Step 2: build the DGM with the calibrated k_treat ───────────────────── dgm_uniform <- do.call(   generate_aft_dgm_flex,   c(base_args_uniform, list(k_treat = k_treat_uniform)) )  t_dgm <- as.numeric(difftime(Sys.time(), .t_dgm_start, units = "secs"))  cat("Uniform DGM (AHR-calibrated)

.t_dgm_start <- Sys.time()  # ── All arguments to generate_aft_dgm_flex() except k_treat ─────────────── # k_treat is the calibration parameter; everything else is fixed up front. base_args_uniform <- list(   # ── Required: source data & outcome ─────────────────────────────────────   data                = gbsg,   continuous_vars     = c("age", "size", "nodes", "pgr", "er"),   factor_vars         = c("meno", "grade"),   outcome_var         = "time_months",   event_var           = "status",   # ── Treatment ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────   treatment_var       = "hormon",   draw_treatment      = FALSE,                                  # default   # ── HTE specification — uniform treatment effect, no embedded subgroup ──   model               = "null",                                 # uniform HR throughout   subgroup_vars       = NULL,                                   # default — no embedded HTE   subgroup_cuts       = NULL,                                   # default   k_inter             = 1,                                      # default (irrelevant under "null")   spline_spec         = NULL,                                   # default   set_beta_spec       = list(set_var = NULL, beta_var = NULL),  # default   # ── Censoring model (independent of treatment effect) ───────────────────   continuous_vars_cens = NULL,                                  # default → inherit   factor_vars_cens     = NULL,                                  # default → inherit   select_censoring     = TRUE,                                  # default — AIC select   cens_type            = "weibull",                             # default   cens_params          = list(),                                # default   cens_intercept_only  = FALSE,                                 # default   # ── Super population & misc ─────────────────────────────────────────────   n_super             = 5000,   standardize         = FALSE,                                  # default   seed                = 99,   verbose             = FALSE )  # ── Step 1: calibrate k_treat so that the AHR is exactly 0.70 ───────────── # We calibrate to the AHR (average hazard ratio over the super-population), # not the marginal Cox HR, because the simulation analyses below fit a Cox # model stratified by `grade` — and under Cox non-collapsibility the # marginal Cox HR on fully-observed potential outcomes is attenuated toward # 1 relative to both the AHR and the stratified Cox HR.  Calibrating to the # AHR makes the simulation median HR track 0.70 closely; calibrating to the # marginal Cox HR (`use_ahr = FALSE`, the default) would pull the simulation # median below 0.70.  See `?calibrate_k_treat` for both options. k_treat_uniform <- calibrate_k_treat(   target_hr_overall = 0.70,   base_args         = base_args_uniform,   k_treat_range     = c(-5, 5),   tol               = 1e-6,   use_ahr           = TRUE,   verbose           = TRUE )  # ── Step 2: build the DGM with the calibrated k_treat ───────────────────── dgm_uniform <- do.call(   generate_aft_dgm_flex,   c(base_args_uniform, list(k_treat = k_treat_uniform)) )  t_dgm <- as.numeric(difftime(Sys.time(), .t_dgm_start, units = "secs"))  cat("Uniform DGM (AHR-calibrated)
",     "  k_treat calibrated to       : ", round(k_treat_uniform, 4), "
",     "  AHR (target 0.70)           : ",     round(dgm_uniform$hazard_ratios$AHR, 4), "
",     "  marginal Cox HR (attenuated): ",     round(dgm_uniform$hazard_ratios$overall, 4), "
",     "  implied median event T      : ",     round(exp(dgm_uniform$model_params$mu), 1), " months
", sep = "") Uniform DGM (AHR-calibrated)   k_treat calibrated to       : 0.956   AHR (target 0.70)           : 0.7   marginal Cox HR (attenuated): 0.7665   implied median event T      : 55.5 months # ── Hard stop: fixed-baseline mode requires dgm$df_source ───────────────── # The whole vignette simulates via baseline = "fixed", which reads the # source frame stored by the constructor (forestsearch versions that # store df_source).  Fail here, at build time, rather than 1,000 lines # later inside the parallel loop. if (is.null(dgm_uniform$df_source)) {   stop("dgm_uniform$df_source is missing: this forestsearch version does ",        "not store the fixed-baseline frame. Update the package ",        "(baseline = "fixed" support) and rebuild the DGM.") } cat("Fixed-baseline panel  : nrow(df_source) =",     nrow(dgm_uniform$df_source), "patients (the GBSG trial data)

title: Extreme Subgroup Effects Under a Uniform Treatment Benefit
text: simulation results credible, censoring pattern synthetic trial must match observed source data. simulated censoring rate much higher lower real one, event counts small subgroups systematically wrong, biasing HR UB(HR) distributions trying characterise. Even well-fitted censoring model, interaction DGM censoring distribution administrative censoring (analysis_time cutoff) can shift effective censoring rate substantially away observed. section covers two functions diagnose correct shift main simulation loop run. simulation pipeline small number parameters govern every per-trial draw: baseline mode, administrative analysis time, recruitment window, iteration-seed scheme. Defining , single sim_config list, means calibration step (), single-trial demonstration Part III, main parallel loop Part IV use exactly values — duplication, risk drift. Change field every downstream chunk reacts automatically. baseline = "fixed" per-trial N free parameter — nrow(dgm_uniform$df_source) construction. check_censoring_dgm() compares three censoring summaries DGM reference data (dgm$df_super) simulated dataset: overall censoring rate, censoring-time quantiles among censored subjects, KM-based median censoring time (estimated reversing event indicator censored observations become “event” interest). Reading output. Flags warn absolute censoring-rate discrepancy exceeds rate_tol (default 10 percentage points) KM median censoring times differ median_tol (default 25%). Common causes: Time-scale mismatch — check exp(dgm$model_params$mu) analysis_time. Short analysis_time — administrative censoring dominates censoring process, inflating censoring rate compressing censoring times. Large cens_adjust — log-scale shift moved DGM censoring distribution far original data. calibrate_cens_adjust() uses uniroot find value cens_adjust — log-scale shift applied DGM censoring model — equates chosen summary statistic reference simulated data. Two targets available: "rate" (overall censoring rate) "km_median" (KM-based median censoring time). objective function works. candidate cens_adjust: simulate_from_dgm() generates n_eval synthetic subjects. check_censoring_dgm() extracts target metric. objective returns sim_metric - ref_metric. uniroot finds zero crossing. fixed seed inside objective ensures candidate always evaluated identically, preventing root-finder chasing Monte Carlo noise. Monotonicity note. objective monotone cens_adjust targets: larger values increase censoring times (lower rate, higher KM median), smaller values opposite. uniroot fails, target lies outside interval; widen retry.

Every downstream # call to simulate_from_dgm() and calibrate_cens_adjust() references this # list — nothing is hard-coded twice. # # baseline = "fixed": every simulated trial uses dgm$df_source (each GBSG # patient exactly once), so per-trial N is nrow(df_source) rather than a # free n_per_trial parameter — n is deliberately absent from this list. sim_config <- list(   baseline         = "fixed",     # conditional-on-X: covariates fixed at trial data   analysis_time    = 84,          # months — administrative censoring time   max_entry        = 24,          # months — uniform recruitment window   seed_base        = 0L,          # per-trial seed = seed_base + iter   rand_seed_offset = 1e6L         # random-subgroup seed = seed + offset )  cat("Per-trial simulation parameters
",     "  baseline      : ", sim_config$baseline,     "  (N per trial = ", nrow(dgm_uniform$df_source),     ", fixed by construction)
",     "  analysis_time :", sim_config$analysis_time, "months
",     "  max_entry     :", sim_config$max_entry,     "months
",     "  seed scheme   : iter seed = ", sim_config$seed_base,     " + ss

code: library(future) library(doFuture) library(foreach)  # By default, target at least 90% of available cores; ceiling() guarantees # the 90% floor on machines where 0.9 * cores is non-integer.  Set # n_workers_user in the User settings chunk to override. .t_par_start  <- Sys.time() n_cores_total <- future::availableCores() n_workers     <- if (is.null(n_workers_user)) {   max(1L, ceiling(0.90 * n_cores_total)) } else {   max(1L, as.integer(n_workers_user)) }  future::plan(future::multisession, workers = n_workers) t_par_setup   <- as.numeric(difftime(Sys.time(), .t_par_start, units = "secs"))  cat(sprintf(   "Parallel plan: multisession with %d workers (%.0f%% of %d available cores).\n",   n_workers, 100 * n_workers / n_cores_total, n_cores_total )) Parallel plan: multisession with 4 workers (100% of 4 available cores). # ── Per-iteration helpers ────────────────────────────────────────────────── # Two pure functions.  Nothing is captured from the outer scope — every # input is passed explicitly — so the %dofuture% body below is a single # line dispatching into run_one_sim().  # Fit a stratified Cox model and return c(HR point estimate, upper 95% CI). cox_sR <- function(data) {   fit <- tryCatch(     coxph(Surv(y_sim, event_sim) ~ treat_sim + strata(grade), data = data),     error = function(e) NULL   )   if (is.null(fit) || nrow(summary(fit)$conf.int) == 0) {     return(c(NA_real_, NA_real_))   }   ci <- summary(fit)$conf.int[1, ]   c(ci["exp(coef)"], ci["upper .95"]) }  # Run one simulated trial and return per-subgroup (HR, UB, N) row vectors. # `cut_points`   list of scalars exposed as columns of df_s so subgroup #                expressions like "age <= age_med" resolve correctly. # `cox_fn`       per-subgroup analysis function — swap for sensitivity #                analyses (unstratified, X+sR, etc.) without touching #                the loop. run_one_sim <- function(ss, dgm, cens_adjust, sim_config,                          subgroups, cut_points, cox_fn) {    # 1. Draw one synthetic trial from the calibrated DGM.   #    baseline = "fixed": the covariate panel is dgm$df_source (every   #    source patient exactly once), identical for every ss — only   #    treatment, entry, event times, and censoring are re-drawn.  n is   #    implied by the panel and deliberately not passed.   df_s <- simulate_from_dgm(     dgm           = dgm,     baseline      = sim_config$baseline,     analysis_time = sim_config$analysis_time,     max_entry     = sim_config$max_entry,     cens_adjust   = cens_adjust,     seed          = sim_config$seed_base + ss   )    # 2. Expose flag_itt and scalar cut-points as columns   df_s$flag_itt <- 1L   for (nm in names(cut_points)) df_s[[nm]] <- cut_points[[nm]]    # 3. Regenerate random-benchmark subgroups for this trial.   #    Membership is re-drawn each replicate, but over the FIXED panel:   #    sizes are exactly 60/40/20/15 every trial (n_s is constant), so the   #    random benchmarks isolate pure membership noise at fixed N.   set.seed(sim_config$seed_base + ss + sim_config$rand_seed_offset)   n_s   <- nrow(df_s)   r_idx <- sample.int(n_s, min(60L, n_s), replace = FALSE)   df_s$random60 <- as.integer(seq_len(n_s) %in% r_idx)   df_s$random40 <- as.integer(seq_len(n_s) %in% r_idx[seq_len(min(40L, length(r_idx)))])   df_s$random20 <- as.integer(seq_len(n_s) %in% r_idx[seq_len(min(20L, length(r_idx)))])   df_s$random15 <- as.integer(seq_len(n_s) %in% r_idx[seq_len(min(15L, length(r_idx)))])    # 4. Fit cox_fn() in every pre-defined subgroup   sg_ids <- vapply(subgroups, `[[`, character(1L), "id")   n_sg   <- length(subgroups)   hr_row <- rep(NA_real_, n_sg)   ub_row <- rep(NA_real_, n_sg)   n_row  <- rep(NA_real_, n_sg)    for (gg in seq_len(n_sg)) {     df_sg <- tryCatch(       subset(df_s, eval(parse(text = sg_ids[[gg]]))),       error = function(e) NULL     )     if (is.null(df_sg) || nrow(df_sg) < 5) next     n_row[gg]  <- nrow(df_sg)     r          <- cox_fn(df_sg)     hr_row[gg] <- r[1]     ub_row[gg] <- r[2]   }    list(hr = hr_row, ub = ub_row, n = n_row) } .t_sims_start <- Sys.time()  # Bundle scalar cut-points into a single argument cut_points <- list(age_med = age_med, size_med = size_med,                     nodes_q3 = nodes_q3, pgr_med = pgr_med, er_cut = er_cut)  # ── Parallel simulation loop ────────────────────────────────────────────── # Each iteration is one call to run_one_sim().  Per-iteration seeding is # handled inside the helper, so .options.future declares seed = NULL. sim_results <- foreach::foreach(   ss = seq_len(n_sims_uniform),   .options.future = list(     seed     = NULL,     packages = c("forestsearch", "survival")   ) ) %dofuture% {   run_one_sim(ss, dgm_uniform, cal_uniform$cens_adjust, sim_config,               subgroups, cut_points, cox_sR) }  # ── Recombine per-iteration results into matrices ───────────────────────── sg_names <- vapply(subgroups, `[[`, character(1L), "name") sim_hrs  <- do.call(rbind, lapply(sim_results, `[[`, "hr")) sim_ubs  <- do.call(rbind, lapply(sim_results, `[[`, "ub")) sim_ns   <- do.call(rbind, lapply(sim_results, `[[`, "n")) colnames(sim_hrs) <- sg_names colnames(sim_ubs) <- sg_names colnames(sim_ns)  <- sg_names  # Release workers (memory hygiene; not strictly required) future::plan(future::sequential)  cat("Simulations completed:", n_sims_uniform,     " |  Parallel workers used:", n_workers, "\n") Simulations completed: 150  |  Parallel workers used: 4 t_sims <- as.numeric(difftime(Sys.time(), .t_sims_start, units = "secs"))

text: main vignette uses uniform-effect DGM (model = "null"): every patient shares true HR = 0.70, apparent subgroup finding false positive. appendix illustrates alternative case — DGM genuine heterogeneous treatment effects (HTE), specific subgroup patients experiences different (smaller larger) treatment effect rest population. generate_aft_dgm_flex() supports HTE via model = "alt" combined subgroup_vars, subgroup_cuts, interaction modifier k_inter. example embeds harm subgroup defined ER-low (er ≤ 20) pre-menopausal (meno == 0) status, interaction strength chosen within-harm-subgroup HR materially attenuated relative -harm complement. Calibration follows procedure Part II — DGM object changes. reuse sim_config per-trial pipeline parameters (analysis_time, max_entry) identical main analysis. Fitting unstratified Cox models within true subgroup recovers embedded heterogeneity — harm subgroup’s observed HR materially higher -harm complement’s.  Kaplan–Meier curves one simulated HTE trial. Harm-subgroup curves diverge less arms -harm complement, reflecting embedded HTE. appendix DGM useful target evaluating subgroup-discovery methods (forestsearch()): know true harm subgroup construction can measure whether method recovers .

title: Exploratory subgroup identification with forestsearch (the 2024 workflow)
text: clinical trials, particularly oncology, subgroup analyses essential : Evaluating treatment effect consistency across patient populations Identifying subgroups treatment may detrimental (harm) Characterizing subgroups enhanced benefit Informing regulatory decisions clinical practice prespecified subgroups provide stronger evidence, important subgroups based patient characteristics may anticipated. ForestSearch provides principled approach exploratory subgroup identification proper statistical inference.

title: Exploratory subgroup identification with forestsearch (the 2024 workflow)
text: ForestSearch identifies subgroups : Candidate factor selection: Using LASSO /Generalized Random Forests (GRF) Exhaustive subgroup search: Evaluating combinations maxk factors Consistency-based selection: Applying splitting consistency criteria Bootstrap bias correction: Adjusting selection-induced optimism Cross-validation: Assessing algorithm stability key innovation splitting consistency criterion: subgroup considered “consistent harm” , randomly split 50/50 many times, halves consistently show hazard ratios ≥ 1.0 (example 1.0 represents meaningful “harm threshold”).

title: Interpretable subgroup identification with forestsearch
text: analysis set 686 patients complete prognostic data, 720 randomized: 246 received hormonal therapy 440 , 299 recurrences deaths. Seven covariates enter search: age, menopausal status, tumour size, grade, number positive lymph nodes, progesterone estrogen receptor concentrations fmol/l. Randomization status masked distributed data; hormonal therapy analysed randomized. Every bound read trial’s effect, hazard ratio 0.695, clinically meaningful effect sizes — test hazard ratio one.
code: df <- survival::gbsg df <- within(df, {   id          <- seq_len(nrow(df))              # the fit's subject identifier   time_months <- rfstime / 30.4375              # recurrence-free survival, days to months   grade3      <- ifelse(grade == "3", 1, 0)     # grade 3 against grade 1 or 2 }) confounders <- c("age", "meno", "size", "grade3", "nodes", "pgr", "er") stopifnot(nrow(df) == 686, sum(df$status) == 299)  whole <- coxph(Surv(time_months, status) ~ hormon, data = df) whole_hr <- c(est = unname(exp(coef(whole))), exp(confint(whole))[1, ]) c(patients = nrow(df), hormonal_therapy = sum(df$hormon == 1),   none = sum(df$hormon == 0), events = sum(df$status)) #>         patients hormonal_therapy             none           events #>              686              246              440              299 sprintf("Whole-trial hazard ratio %.3f (%.3f, %.3f), hormonal therapy vs none",         whole_hr[["est"]], whole_hr[[2]], whole_hr[[3]]) #> [1] "Whole-trial hazard ratio 0.695 (0.544, 0.888), hormonal therapy vs none"

text: Guo ’s Section 5.2 generates n=400n = 400 subjects W∼Unif[0,80]W \sim \mathrm{Unif}[0, 80] treatment D∼Bernoulli(0.5)D \sim \mathrm{Bernoulli}(0.5) proportional hazards model λ0(t)exp⁡{b(W)D}\lambda_0(t)\exp\{b(W)D\} unit exponential baseline hazard, b(w)=β2b(w) = \beta_2 w≤30w \le 30 00 otherwise, censoring log⁡C∼Unif(−1.25,1.00)\log C \sim \mathrm{Unif}(-1.25, 1.00), 40% across cells; β2∈{0,0.1,…,0.5}\beta_2 \\{0, 0.1, \ldots, 0.5\}. true harm region H={W≤30}H = \{W \le 30\}, 150 subjects. candidates S(c)={W≤c}S(c) = \{W \le c\} c∈[30,60]c \[30, 60]. estimate changes cc passes observed value WW, family taken distinct cuts 30 every observed w∈(30,60]w \(30, 60] — nested, cut every observed value, 151 candidates per replicate. discretisation manuscript’s; Guo state one. One trial, see objects:
code: W_MAX <- 80; C_LO <- 30; C_HI <- 60  # One trial under the Section 5.2 design. sim_data <- function(beta2, n) {   w <- runif(n, 0, W_MAX)   d <- rbinom(n, 1L, 0.5)   b <- ifelse(w <= C_LO, beta2, 0)   t_event <- rexp(n, rate = exp(b * d))   t_cens  <- exp(runif(n, -1.25, 1.00))   data.frame(time = pmin(t_event, t_cens), event = as.integer(t_event <= t_cens),              treat = d, w = w) }  # The nested family: one 0/1 membership column per distinct cutpoint, and the # same family as a list of row indices (the form fs_mr_inference() takes). nested_family <- function(df) {   cuts <- c(C_LO, sort(df$w[df$w > C_LO & df$w <= C_HI]))   nm   <- sprintf("cand_%03d", seq_along(cuts))   memb <- vapply(cuts, function(cc) as.integer(df$w <= cc), integer(nrow(df)))   colnames(memb) <- nm   list(df = cbind(df, as.data.frame(memb)), cuts = cuts, names = nm,        members = stats::setNames(lapply(seq_along(cuts),                                         function(j) which(memb[, j] == 1L)), nm)) }  # The standard analysis of every candidate: the treatment-only Cox fit within # S(c), its coefficient and model-based standard error. family_fits <- function(fam) {   k <- length(fam$names)   est <- se <- rep(NA_real_, k)   for (j in seq_len(k)) {     sub <- fam$df[fam$members[[j]], , drop = FALSE]     fit <- try(suppressWarnings(       survival::coxph(survival::Surv(time, event) ~ treat, data = sub)), silent = TRUE)     if (!inherits(fit, "try-error")) {       est[j] <- unname(coef(fit)[[1L]])       se[j]  <- unname(sqrt(vcov(fit)[1L, 1L]))     }   }   list(est = est, se = se) }  # The identifier: the pure argmax of the raw coefficient, Guo and He's # selection. Larger beta is the effect of interest, and beta(c) is a log hazard # ratio, so the argmax picks the subgroup with the largest estimated hazard # ratio -- forest search's harm-side argmax, with no sign change. argmax_candidate <- function(fits) which.max(replace(fits$est, !is.finite(fits$est), -Inf)) set.seed(1) df1  <- sim_data(0.3, 400L) fam1 <- nested_family(df1) fits1 <- family_fits(fam1) sel1 <- argmax_candidate(fits1) c(candidates = length(fam1$cuts), censoring = round(mean(df1$event == 0), 3),   c_hat = round(fam1$cuts[sel1], 2), n_selected = length(fam1$members[[sel1]]),   beta_hat = round(fits1$est[sel1], 3)) #> candidates  censoring      c_hat n_selected   beta_hat #>    152.000      0.412     58.340    301.000     -0.028

Two facts anchor : β(30)=β2\beta(30) = \beta_2 exactly, bb constant [0,30][0, 30]; β(c)\beta(c) non-increasing c>30c > 30, diluted null region alone. β2=0\beta_2 = 0 curve exactly zero everywhere. β2>0\beta_2 > 0 closed form, curve computed one large sample prefix sweep grid cc, isotonic non-increasing projection interpolation basis. manuscript uses nbig=2×106n_{\mathrm{big}} = 2 \times 10^6 0.25 grid; article uses 200,000 unit grid, costs seconds places β(c)\beta(c) within 0.006 manuscript’s curve. truth curve cell (n_big = 200,000; 16.8 s).
code: truth_curve <- function(beta2, n_big, c_step = 1, seed) {   set.seed(seed)   df <- sim_data(beta2, n_big)   df <- df[order(df$w), , drop = FALSE]   c_grid <- seq(C_LO, C_HI, by = c_step)   n_sub  <- findInterval(c_grid, df$w)   beta_raw <- se <- numeric(length(c_grid))   for (j in seq_along(c_grid)) {     sub <- df[seq_len(n_sub[j]), , drop = FALSE]     fit <- survival::coxph(survival::Surv(time, event) ~ treat, data = sub,                            model = FALSE, x = FALSE, y = FALSE)     beta_raw[j] <- unname(coef(fit)[[1L]])     se[j] <- unname(sqrt(vcov(fit)[1L, 1L]))   }   beta_smooth <- -stats::isoreg(c_grid, -beta_raw)$yf   # non-increasing projection   list(beta2 = beta2, n_big = n_big, c_grid = c_grid, beta_raw = beta_raw, se = se,        beta = if (beta2 == 0) rep(0, length(c_grid)) else beta_smooth,        anchor_dev = beta_raw[1] - beta2) } truth_at <- function(tr, c_hat) stats::approx(tr$c_grid, tr$beta, xout = c_hat, rule = 2)$y  t0 <- proc.time()[["elapsed"]] truth <- lapply(cells, function(b2)   truth_curve(b2, n_big = n_big, c_step = 1, seed = 20260721L + as.integer(round(100 * b2)))) names(truth) <- sprintf("%.1f", cells) truth_sec <- proc.time()[["elapsed"]] - t0 knitr::kable(data.frame(   beta2 = cells,   `beta(30), estimated` = sapply(truth, function(tr) sprintf("%.4f", tr$beta_raw[1])),   `anchor deviation / SE` = sapply(truth, function(tr) sprintf("%.2f", tr$anchor_dev / tr$se[1])),   `beta(60)` = sapply(truth, function(tr) sprintf("%.4f", tr$beta[length(tr$beta)])),   basis = sapply(truth, function(tr) if (tr$beta2 == 0) "exact zero" else "isotonic projection"),   check.names = FALSE), row.names = FALSE,   caption = sprintf("The truth curve by cell (n_big = %s; %.1f s).",                     format(n_big, big.mark = ",", scientific = FALSE), truth_sec))

code: seed_base <- function(beta2)   1000000L + as.integer(sum(utf8ToInt(sprintf("t7_beta2_%02d", as.integer(round(10 * beta2)))))) * 100003L  mr_spec <- list(outcome_type = "survival", effect_measure = "HR", treat.name = "treat",                 outcome.name = "time", event.name = "event", offset.name = NULL,                 adjust_covariates = NULL, adverse_outcome = NULL)  # One replicate: the trial, the family, the selection, the truth at the selected # cutpoint, and every bound. All bounds are returned on the log hazard-ratio # scale; exp() gives the hazard-ratio scale used in the tables. bounds_one <- function(beta2, m, tr, B_gh, mr_draws, R_out, R_in) {   base <- seed_base(beta2)   set.seed(base + m)   df   <- sim_data(beta2, 400L)   fam  <- nested_family(df)   fits <- family_fits(fam)   sel  <- argmax_candidate(fits)   in_H <- fam$members[[sel]]   c_hat <- fam$cuts[sel]   gamma <- truth_at(tr, c_hat)                        # beta(H-hat), the target   fit_c <- survival::coxph(survival::Surv(time, event) ~ treat,                            data = fam$df[-in_H, , drop = FALSE], robust = TRUE)   gh <- guohe_algorithm3(     data = fam$df, outcome = "survival", treatment = "treat", candidates = fam$names,     time = "time", event = "event", orient = +1, B = B_gh, r = 1 / 12, level = 0.05,     seed = base + m + 500000L, min_events = 5L, diagnostics = FALSE)   mr <- fs_mr_inference(     df = fam$df, candidates = fam$members, spec = mr_spec, selected_members = in_H,     admission = list(effect_floor = NULL, consistency = NULL),   # no screen: the pure argmax     reselection = "maxeff", draws = mr_draws, multiplier = "poisson",     ci_method = "field", seed = base + m + 700000L,     include_complement = TRUE, field_R_out = R_out, field_R_in = R_in,     field_complement = TRUE, field_scale_complement = "selected")   data.frame(     beta2 = beta2, m = m, k = length(fam$cuts), c_hat = c_hat, n_sel = length(in_H),     gamma = gamma,     gh_sel_agree = identical(gh$selected, fam$names[sel]),     mr_sel_agree = identical(as.integer(mr$selected_index), as.integer(sel)),     # the selected subgroup: point estimate and one-sided 95% lower bound, four ways     un_est  = fits$est[sel],            un_lower  = fits$est[sel] - z95 * fits$se[sel],     gh_est  = log(gh$debiased),         gh_lower  = log(gh$bound_one_sided),     fld_est = log(mr$field$est2),       fld_lower = log(mr$field$lower_1s),     ij_est  = log(mr$debiased$est),     ij_lower  = log(mr$debiased$lower_1s),     p_hat_H = unname(mr$reselection$p_hat[sel]),     # the complement: one-sided 95% upper bounds, and the pair at 0.975 a side     c_un_upper  = unname(coef(fit_c)[[1L]]) + z95 * unname(sqrt(fit_c$var[1L, 1L])),     c_ij_upper  = log(mr$complement$debiased$est) + z95 * mr$complement$debiased$se_ij,     c_fld_upper = log(mr$field$complement$upper_1s_s),     pair_lower_H  = log(mr$field$joint_s$bonf_lower_H),     pair_upper_Hc = log(mr$field$joint_s$bonf_upper_Hc)) } tr_walk <- if ("0.3" %in% names(truth)) truth[["0.3"]] else   truth_curve(0.3, n_big = n_big, c_step = 1, seed = 20260721L + 30L) t0 <- proc.time()[["elapsed"]] one <- bounds_one(0.3, 1L, tr_walk, B_gh = 2000L, mr_draws = 5000L, R_out = 1000L, R_in = 500L) one_sec <- proc.time()[["elapsed"]] - t0 f2 <- function(x) sprintf("%.2f", exp(x)) walk <- data.frame(   quantity = c("selected cutpoint c-hat (true boundary 30)", "selected subgroup |H-hat| (H is about 150)",                "hazard ratio in H-hat, the target exp{beta(H-hat)}",                "unadjusted: estimate, 95% lower bound",                "Guo-He r = 1/12: bias-reduced estimate, 95% lower bound",                "MR (field): estimate, 95% lower bound",                "MR (IJ two-term): estimate, 95% lower bound",                "re-selection frequency p-hat(H-hat)",                "complement, 95% upper bound: unadjusted / IJ two-term / field-s",                "Bonferroni pair: lower on H-hat / upper on H-hat^c (0.975 a side)"),   value = c(sprintf("%.1f", one$c_hat), sprintf("%d of 400", one$n_sel), f2(one$gamma),             sprintf("%s, %s", f2(one$un_est), f2(one$un_lower)),             sprintf("%s, %s", f2(one$gh_est), f2(one$gh_lower)),             sprintf("%s, %s", f2(one$fld_est), f2(one$fld_lower)),             sprintf("%s, %s", f2(one$ij_est), f2(one$ij_lower)),             sprintf("%.3f", one$p_hat_H),             sprintf("%s / %s / %s", f2(one$c_un_upper), f2(one$c_ij_upper), f2(one$c_fld_upper)),             sprintf("%s / %s", f2(one$pair_lower_H), f2(one$pair_upper_Hc)))) knitr::kable(walk, col.names = c("", "hazard-ratio scale"), row.names = FALSE,              caption = sprintf("Replicate 1, beta_2 = 0.3, at the manuscript's settings (%d candidates; %.0f s).",                                one$k, one_sec))

code: run_cell <- function(beta2, tr) {   t0 <- proc.time()[["elapsed"]]   rows <- future_lapply(seq_len(n_rep), function(m)     bounds_one(beta2, m, tr, B_gh = B_gh, mr_draws = mr_draws, R_out = R_out, R_in = R_in),     future.seed = TRUE, future.packages = c("forestsearch", "survival"))   res <- do.call(rbind, rows)   attr(res, "seconds") <- proc.time()[["elapsed"]] - t0   res } if (n_workers > 1L) plan(multisession, workers = n_workers) else plan(sequential) res <- lapply(cells, function(b2) run_cell(b2, truth[[sprintf("%.1f", b2)]])) plan(sequential) names(res) <- sprintf("%.1f", cells) cell_sec <- sapply(res, attr, "seconds") stopifnot(all(sapply(res, function(r) all(r$gh_sel_agree & r$mr_sel_agree)))) wilson <- function(x, n, z = qnorm(0.975)) {   p <- x / n; den <- 1 + z^2 / n   ctr <- (p + z^2 / (2 * n)) / den   hw  <- z * sqrt(p * (1 - p) / n + z^2 / (4 * n^2)) / den   c(lo = ctr - hw, hi = ctr + hw) } LOWER_METHODS <- c("Unadjusted" = "un", "Guo-He r = 1/12" = "gh",                    "MR (field)" = "fld", "MR (IJ two-term)" = "ij") summarise_lower <- function(r) {   do.call(rbind, lapply(names(LOWER_METHODS), function(nm) {     p <- LOWER_METHODS[[nm]]     est <- r[[paste0(p, "_est")]]; low <- r[[paste0(p, "_lower")]]     cov <- low <= r$gamma; n <- nrow(r); w <- wilson(sum(cov), n)     data.frame(beta2 = r$beta2[1], method = nm, n = n,                coverage = mean(cov), wilson_lo = w[["lo"]], wilson_hi = w[["hi"]],                margin = mean(est - code: # Power approximation function approx_power <- function(hr, n_subgroup, cens_rate = 0.45) {   beta <- log(hr)   d <- (1 - cens_rate) * n_subgroup   var_split <- 8 / d    # Numerical integration   integrate_2d <- function(beta, var) {     # Use Monte Carlo integration     set.seed(123)     n_sim <- 100000     w1 <- rnorm(n_sim, mean = beta, sd = sqrt(var))     w2 <- rnorm(n_sim, mean = beta, sd = sqrt(var))      mean((w1 + w2 >= 2 * log(1.25)) & (w1 >= 0) & (w2 >= 0))   }    integrate_2d(beta, var_split) }  # Calculate power curves hr_seq <- seq(0.5, 3.0, by = 0.05) n_values <- c(60, 80, 100)  power_data <- expand.grid(hr = hr_seq, n = n_values) power_data$power <- mapply(approx_power, power_data$hr, power_data$n) power_data$n <- factor(power_data$n, labels = paste("n =", n_values))  library(ggplot2) ggplot(power_data, aes(x = hr, y = power, color = n)) +   geom_line(linewidth = 1) +   geom_hline(yintercept = 0.10, linetype = "dashed", color = "gray50") +   geom_hline(yintercept = 0.80, linetype = "dashed", color = "gray50") +   geom_vline(xintercept = 1.0, linetype = "dotted", color = "gray70") +   scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0.5, 3.0, by = 0.5)) +   scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 1, by = 0.2), labels = scales::percent) +   labs(     x = "Underlying Hazard Ratio",     y = "Probability of Identifying H",     color = "Subgroup Size",     title = "ForestSearch Power Approximation",     subtitle = "Censoring rate ~= 45%"   ) +   theme_minimal() +   theme(legend.position = "bottom") +   annotate("text", x = 0.6, y = 0.12, label = "10% threshold", size = 3) +   annotate("text", x = 0.6, y = 0.82, label = "80% power", size = 3)

text: section outlines end--end workflow evaluating ForestSearch performance via simulation. step described workflow diagram, cross-references corresponding vignette sections.    Four-stage simulation workflow evaluating subgroup identification performance.  DGM defines ground truth simulation. Building GBSG breast cancer dataset covariate template, setup_gbsg_dgm() fits Accelerated Failure Time (AFT) model Weibull baseline hazard generates super-population potential outcomes. Key decisions stage: Hypothesis: model = "alt" introduces treatment effect heterogeneity (harm subgroup H vs. benefit complement Hc); model = "null" imposes uniform treatment effect true subgroup exists (type-error evaluation). Effect size: k_inter parameter scales treatment--covariate interaction. Rather setting manually, use calibrate_k_inter() find value achieves target HR harm subgroup, calibrated either Cox HR (use_ahr = FALSE) average hazard ratio (use_ahr = TRUE). Subgroup definition: default, H = {low estrogen receptor premenopausal} (z1 = 1 & z3 = 1), covering roughly 13% super-population. Censoring: Weibull uniform censoring, optionally adjusted via cens_adjust control overall event rate. resulting DGM object stores super-population, true hazard ratios (Cox-based AHR), individual-level potential outcomes (loghr_po), model parameters needed downstream simulation. simulate_from_dgm() draws random samples super-population create synthetic trial datasets. simulated trial: Samples n patients (e.g., 700) 1:1 randomisation. Generates survival times AFT model using DGM parameters. Applies censoring (Weibull uniform, optional cens_adjust adjustment) administrative censoring analysis_time. Carries forward true subgroup indicator flag_harm individual loghr_po evaluation. simulated trial independent replicate full analysis pipeline. consistency screen within evaluated closed form (consistency_method = "resample", default; 2026b, Section 2.2), fs.splits effect runs unless closed form unavailable candidate. run_simulation_analysis() wraps ForestSearch algorithm (optionally GRF) returns one-row-per-method summary replicate. typical call enables one methods: method function records whether subgroup identified (.H), composition (sens, spec, ppv, npv), hazard ratio estimates (hr.H.hat, hr.Hc.hat), AHR estimates (ahr.H.hat, ahr.Hc.hat), subgroup size, timing. simulation loop parallelised via foreach / doFuture (see Setting Parallel Processing): Three complementary summary functions distil raw simulation output interpretable results: format_oc_results() produces gt table operating characteristics (detection rate, sensitivity, specificity, PPV, NPV, mean HR estimates) across analysis methods, selectable metric groups ("detection", "classification", "hr_estimates", "ahr_estimates", "subgroup_size", ""). build_estimation_table() focuses estimation bias: estimator (naive Cox HR, bias-corrected HR, AHR) H Hc, reports mean, SD, range, relative bias versus DGM truth. CDE values available, dual bias columns (b‡ vs CDE, b† vs marginal HR) shown, matching notation Table 5 Leon et al. (2024). bias-corrected rows bootstrap correction 2024 workflow, shown hr.H.bc / hr.Hc.bc columns present; multiplier-resampling estimate one-sided bounds current inference among columns run_simulation_analysis() records, operating characteristics reported 2026b (Section 5 Supplementary Section S2) 2026a (Section 7 Supplementary Section S8). build_classification_table() assembles detection classification rates across multiple DGM scenarios (e.g., null alternative) single table, facilitating comparison published benchmarks Leon et al. (2024). Additionally, interpret_estimation_table() generates templated narrative paragraph auto-populates numerical results, suitable direct inclusion reports via results = "asis". sections follow implement step detail. compact version full workflow (excluding diagnostics) : structured timing framework tracks computational cost stage simulation study. initialize named list accumulates elapsed times DGM creation, calibration, validation, simulation loops H1 H0, summarization, table formatting.

dgm$hazard_ratios <- list(   overall          = hr_causal,      # Cox-based overall HR   AHR              = AHR,            # Average HR from loghr_po    AHR_harm         = AHR_H_true,     # AHR in harm subgroup   AHR_no_harm      = AHR_Hc_true,    # AHR in complement   harm_subgroup    = hr_H_true,      # Cox-based HR in H   no_harm_subgroup = hr_Hc_true,     # Cox-based HR in Hc    # Controlled Direct Effects (CDE) — see treatment_effect_definitions vignette    CDE              = CDE_overall,    # Overall CDE   CDE_harm         = CDE_H,         # CDE in harm subgroup   (theta-ddagger(H))   CDE_no_harm      = CDE_Hc         # CDE in complement      (theta-ddagger(Hc)) ) # One-line creation of the León et al. (2024) simulation DGM dgm <- setup_gbsg_dgm(   model   = "alt",    # "alt" (heterogeneous effects) or "null"   k_inter = 2.5,      # treatment × subgroup interaction strength   k_treat = 1.0,      # overall treatment effect modifier   seed    = 8316951 ) library(forestsearch) library(survival)   # for survival::gbsg  # ── Step 1: Prepare the GBSG dataset ──────────────────────────────────────  dfa <- survival::gbsg  # Convert time to months (matching León et al.) dfa$y     <- dfa$rfstime / 30.4375 dfa$treat <- dfa$hormon  # Subgroup-defining binary variables # H = {ER ≤ 25th percentile} ∩ {premenopausal} er_cut <- quantile(dfa$er, probs = 0.25) dfa$z1 <- as.factor(ifelse(dfa$er  <= er_cut, 1L, 0L))  # ER low dfa$z2 <- as.factor(ifelse(dfa$age <= median(dfa$age), 1L, 0L)) dfa$z3 <- as.factor(ifelse(dfa$meno == 0, 1L, 0L))       # premenopausal dfa$z4 <- as.factor(ifelse(dfa$pgr  <= median(dfa$pgr), 1L, 0L)) dfa$z5 <- as.factor(ifelse(dfa$nodes <= median(dfa$nodes), 1L, 0L)) dfa$v6 <- as.factor(ifelse(dfa$size  <= median(dfa$size), 1L, 0L)) dfa$v7 <- as.factor(ifelse(dfa$grade == 3, 1L, 0L))  # ── Step 2: Call generate_aft_dgm_flex() ──────────────────────────────────  dgm_flex <- generate_aft_dgm_flex(   data            = dfa,   outcome_var     = "y",   event_var       = "status",   treatment_var   = "treat",   # title: setup_gbsg_dgm() and generate_aft_dgm_flex(): Relationship and Usage
text: setup_gbsg_dgm() function creates data generating mechanism (DGM) based Accelerated Failure Time (AFT) model Weibull distribution. Key features: Covariates: Age, estrogen receptor, menopausal status, progesterone receptor, nodes Treatment effect heterogeneity: Specified via interaction terms Subgroup definition: H = {low estrogen receptor premenopausal} Censoring: Weibull uniform censoring model DGM now includes: CDE ratio average hazard contributions natural scale: CDE(S) = mean(exp(theta_1_i)) / mean(exp(theta_0_i)), differs AHR = exp(mean(loghr_po)) due Jensen’s inequality. paper’s notation, CDE corresponds θ‡ (theta-double-dagger), marginal (causal) HR corresponds θ† (theta-dagger). two targets define dual bias columns Table 5 Leon et al. (2024). super-population data (dgm$df_super_rand) now contains:
code: dgm$hazard_ratios <- list(   overall          = hr_causal,      # Cox-based overall HR   AHR              = AHR,            # Average HR from loghr_po    AHR_harm         = AHR_H_true,     # AHR in harm subgroup   AHR_no_harm      = AHR_Hc_true,    # AHR in complement   harm_subgroup    = hr_H_true,      # Cox-based HR in H   no_harm_subgroup = hr_Hc_true,     # Cox-based HR in Hc    # Controlled Direct Effects (CDE) — see treatment_effect_definitions vignette    CDE              = CDE_overall,    # Overall CDE   CDE_harm         = CDE_H,         # CDE in harm subgroup   (theta-ddagger(H))   CDE_no_harm      = CDE_Hc         # CDE in complement      (theta-ddagger(Hc)) )

title: setup_gbsg_dgm() and generate_aft_dgm_flex(): Relationship and Usage
text: generate_aft_dgm_flex() general DGM builder. requires analyst supply dataset make every modelling choice explicitly. GBSG DGM setup_gbsg_dgm() equivalent following call — simply automates preparation: setup_gbsg_dgm() preferred GBSG simulation setting guarantees exact replication León et al. (2024) covariate construction subgroup definition without requiring analyst reproduce preparation steps hand.
code: library(forestsearch) library(survival)   # for survival::gbsg  # ── Step 1: Prepare the GBSG dataset ──────────────────────────────────────  dfa <- survival::gbsg  # Convert time to months (matching León et al.) dfa$y     <- dfa$rfstime / 30.4375 dfa$treat <- dfa$hormon  # Subgroup-defining binary variables # H = {ER ≤ 25th percentile} ∩ {premenopausal} er_cut <- quantile(dfa$er, probs = 0.25) dfa$z1 <- as.factor(ifelse(dfa$er  <= er_cut, 1L, 0L))  # ER low dfa$z2 <- as.factor(ifelse(dfa$age <= median(dfa$age), 1L, 0L)) dfa$z3 <- as.factor(ifelse(dfa$meno == 0, 1L, 0L))       # premenopausal dfa$z4 <- as.factor(ifelse(dfa$pgr  <= median(dfa$pgr), 1L, 0L)) dfa$z5 <- as.factor(ifelse(dfa$nodes <= median(dfa$nodes), 1L, 0L)) dfa$v6 <- as.factor(ifelse(dfa$size  <= median(dfa$size), 1L, 0L)) dfa$v7 <- as.factor(ifelse(dfa$grade == 3, 1L, 0L))  # ── Step 2: Call generate_aft_dgm_flex() ──────────────────────────────────  dgm_flex <- generate_aft_dgm_flex(   data            = dfa,   outcome_var     = "y",   event_var       = "status",   treatment_var   = "treat",   # Analyst-visible covariates (what FS will search over)   continuous_vars = character(0),    # all pre-discretised   factor_vars     = c("z1", "z2", "z3", "z4", "z5", "v6", "v7"),   # Subgroup definition: H = {z1 = 1} ∩ {z3 = 1}   subgroup_vars   = c("z1", "z3"),   subgroup_cuts   = list(z1 = 1, z3 = 1),   # both must equal 1   # Treatment effect structure   model   = "alt",   k_inter = 2.5,   k_treat = 1.0,   n_super = 5000,   seed    = 8316951 )

# Configure parallel backend n_workers <- min(parallel::detectCores() - 1, 120)  plan(multisession, workers = n_workers)  cat("Using", n_workers, "parallel workers
") Using 3 parallel workers # Simulation settings sim_config_alt <- list(   n_sims = nsims_alt,          # Number of simulations (use 500-1000 for final)   n_sample = 700,         # Sample size per trial   analysis_time = 84,        # Maximum follow-up (months)   seed_base = 8316951,   cens_adjust = log(1.5) )  sim_config_null <- list(   n_sims = nsims_null,          # More simulations for Type I error estimation   n_sample = 700,         # Sample size per trial   analysis_time = 84,        # Maximum follow-up (months)   seed_base = 8316951,   cens_adjust = log(1.5) )  # ForestSearch parameters (now includes use_twostage) fs_params <- list(   outcome.name = "y_sim",   event.name = "event_sim",   treat.name = "treat_sim",   id.name = "id",   use_lasso = TRUE,   use_grf = TRUE,   hr.threshold = 1.25,   hr.consistency = 1.0,   pconsistency.threshold = 0.90,   fs.splits = 400,   n.min = 60,   d0.min = 12,   d1.min = 12,   maxk = 2,   by.risk = 12,   # NEW: Two-stage algorithm option   use_twostage = TRUE,      # Set TRUE for faster exploratory analysis   twostage_args = list(),    # Optional tuning parameters   # Run inner forestsearch() sequentially.  This is the default set by   # default_sim_params() (as of forestsearch v0.2.0) -- restated here so   # the safety pattern is visible to readers of the vignette.  The outer   # foreach() %dofuture% block provides parallelism across simulations;   # the inner forestsearch() therefore runs single-threaded inside each   # worker.  Overriding this back to multisession would re-introduce   # nested parallelism (parallelly's 300%-load hard limit) and is rarely   # what you want inside a foreach() loop.  See   # ?run_simulation_analysis for details ("Parallel Processing" section).   parallel_args = list(plan = "sequential") )   # Confounders for analysis confounders_base <- c("z1", "z2", "z3", "z4", "z5", "size", "grade3") # Fast configuration with two-stage algorithm fs_params_fast <- modifyList(fs_params, list(   use_twostage = TRUE,   twostage_args = list(     n.splits.screen = 30,    # Stage 1 screening splits     batch.size = 20,         # Stage 2 batch size     conf.level = 0.95        # Early stopping confidence   ) ))  cat("Standard search: use_twostage =", fs_params$use_twostage, "

This is the default set by   # default_sim_params() (as of forestsearch v0.2.0) -- restated here so   # the safety pattern is visible to readers of the vignette.  The outer   # foreach() %dofuture% block provides parallelism across simulations;   # the inner forestsearch() therefore runs single-threaded inside each   # worker.  Overriding this back to multisession would re-introduce   # nested parallelism (parallelly's 300%-load hard limit) and is rarely   # what you want inside a foreach() loop. text: format_oc_results() function flexible tool creating publication-quality tables simulation results. accepts raw data.table produced run_simulation_analysis() (combined via rbind / rbindlist across simulations) returns either gt table object plain data.frame. metrics = "", returned table contains one row per analysis method following columns: Pattern 1: Quick summary single simulation run Pattern 2: Compare specific analysis methods Pattern 3: Focus classification metrics Pattern 4: Extract data.frame custom processing Pattern 5: Multiple scenarios side--side Pattern 6: Combine summarize_simulation_results() detailed output summarize_simulation_results() returns data.frame row names like .H, sens, spec, etc. (summarize_single_analysis()), one column per analysis method. useful programmatic access raw summary statistics, format_oc_results() oriented toward presentation-quality tables:
code: format_oc_results(   results,   analyses = NULL,   metrics = "all",   digits = 3,   digits_hr = 3,   title = "Operating Characteristics Summary",   subtitle = NULL,   use_gt = TRUE ) # After running simulations format_oc_results(results_alt, title = "H1 Results") # Compare only FS and GRF format_oc_results(   results_alt,   analyses = c("FS", "GRF"),   title = "FS vs GRF Comparison" ) format_oc_results(   results_alt,   metrics = "classification",   title = "Classification Performance" ) # Get raw summary data.frame for further manipulation oc_df <- format_oc_results(results_alt, use_gt = FALSE)  # Use for custom plotting or LaTeX export # Create tables for different sample sizes or HR targets for (scenario in names(results_list)) {   cat("\n", scenario, "\n")   print(format_oc_results(     results_list[[scenario]],     title = scenario,     subtitle = sprintf("n = %d", sample_sizes[[scenario]])   )) } # Detailed numeric summary (for computation) summary_df <- summarize_simulation_results(results_alt)  # Presentation table (for reports) format_oc_results(results_alt, title = "Publication Table")

") cat("Two-stage algorithm power:", round(mean(results_twostage$any.H), 3), "
") # Run simulations with noise variables results_noise <- foreach(   sim = 1:sim_config_alt$n_sims,   .combine = rbind,   .errorhandling = "remove",   .options.future = list(     packages = c("forestsearch", "survival", "data.table"),     seed = TRUE   ) ) %dofuture% {      run_simulation_analysis(     sim_id = sim,     dgm = dgm_calibrated,     n_sample = sim_config_alt$n_sample,     confounders_base = confounders_base,     n_add_noise = 10,  # Add 10 noise variables     run_fs = TRUE,     fs_params = fs_params,     verbose = FALSE   ) }  # Compare detection rates cat("Without noise:", round(mean(results_alt$any.H), 3), "
") cat("With 10 noise vars:", round(mean(results_noise$any.H), 3), "
") # Test different HR thresholds thresholds <- c(1.10, 1.25, 1.50) results_by_thresh <- list()  for (thresh in thresholds) {   results_by_thresh[[as.character(thresh)]] <- foreach(     sim = 1:100,     .combine = rbind,     .options.future = list(       packages = c("forestsearch", "survival", "data.table"),       seed = TRUE     )   ) %dofuture% {          run_simulation_analysis(       sim_id = sim,       dgm = dgm_calibrated,       n_sample = sim_config_alt$n_sample,       confounders_base = confounders_base,       run_fs = TRUE,       fs_params = modifyList(fs_params, list(hr.threshold = thresh)),       verbose = FALSE     )   }   results_by_thresh[[as.character(thresh)]]$threshold <- thresh }  # Combine and summarize combined <- rbindlist(results_by_thresh) combined[, .(power = mean(any.H), ppv = mean(ppv, na.rm = TRUE)),           by = .(threshold, analysis)]

code: res <- as.data.table(results) res <- res[analysis == analysis_method]   # keep only the requested method res_found <- res[any.H == 1]             # keep only sims that found a subgroup n_estimable <- nrow(res_found) is_null <- (dgm$model_type == "null") ||            (is.na(theta_H_true) && !is.na(theta_Hc_true)) hr_overall  <- get_dgm_hr(dgm, "hr_overall")  # tries hazard_ratios$overall if (is.na(hr_overall)) hr_overall <- dgm$hr_causal  # fallback to direct field  theta_H_true  <- hr_overall   # e.g., 0.72 theta_Hc_true <- hr_overall   # same value under the null make_est_row <- function(estimates, true_val, label, cde_val = NA_real_) {   est <- estimates[!is.na(estimates)]   # drop any NA estimates   if (length(est) == 0) return(NULL)    avg_est  <- mean(est)   sd_est   <- sd(est)   min_est  <- min(est)   max_est  <- max(est)    # b-dagger: bias relative to marginal (causal) truth   b_dagger <- 100 * (avg_est - true_val) / true_val    row <- data.frame(     Estimator    = label,     Avg          = round(avg_est, digits),     SD           = round(sd_est, digits),     Min          = round(min_est, digits),     Max          = round(max_est, digits)   )    if (has_cde && !is.na(cde_val)) {     # b-ddagger: bias relative to CDE truth     b_ddagger <- 100 * (avg_est - cde_val) / cde_val     row[["b-ddagger (%)"]] <- round(b_ddagger, digits)     row[["b-dagger (%)"]]  <- round(b_dagger, digits)   } else {     row[["b-dagger (%)"]]  <- round(b_dagger, digits)   }   row } b† (%)  = 100 * (mean(theta-hat) - theta†) / theta†     [marginal truth] b‡ (%)  = 100 * (mean(theta-hat) - theta‡) / theta‡     [CDE truth]

") cat("AHR (harm):   ", round(ahr_harm, 4), "
") cat("AHR (Hc):     ", round(ahr_noharm, 4), "
")  # --- CDE (deterministic, from theta_0 and theta_1) --- cde_overall <- mean(exp(df$theta_1)) / mean(exp(df$theta_0)) cde_harm    <- mean(exp(df$theta_1[df$flag_harm == 1])) /                mean(exp(df$theta_0[df$flag_harm == 1])) cde_noharm  <- mean(exp(df$theta_1[df$flag_harm == 0])) /                mean(exp(df$theta_0[df$flag_harm == 0]))  cat("CDE (overall):", round(cde_overall, 4), "
") cat("CDE (harm):   ", round(cde_harm, 4), "

") cat("HR_marg (overall):", round(dgm$hr_causal, 4), "

")  # --- Simulation-level truth (per-replicate, observed data) --- cat("

") cat("hr.Hc.true (this replicate):", round(hr_Hc_sim, 4), "
") cat("

Model-based identifiers can propose candidates instead: DINA (subgroup_method = "dina") causal forests (subgroup_method = "grf"). regions re-ranked coefficient receive inference, conditional candidate family propose. full bootstrap correction cross-validation León et al. (2024) remain available. title: Bootstrap Results for ForestSearch with Bias Correction — bootstrap_results
text: Two bias correction approaches implemented: Method 1 (Simple Optimism): $$H_{adj1} = H_{obs} - (H^*_{*} - H^*_{obs})$$ \(H^*_{*}\) new subgroup HR bootstrap data \(H^*_{obs}\) new subgroup HR original data. Method 2 (Double Bootstrap): $$H_{adj2} = 2 \times H_{obs} - (H_{*} + H^*_{*} - H^*_{obs})$$ \(H_{*}\) original subgroup HR bootstrap data. : H_obs: Original subgroup HR original data H_star: Original subgroup HR bootstrap data Hstar_obs: New subgroup (found bootstrap) HR original data Hstar_star: New subgroup (found bootstrap) HR bootstrap data

text: Uses paper's notation conventions: theta-dagger: Marginal (causal) HR truth theta-ddagger: Controlled direct effect (CDE) truth theta-hat(H-hat): Plugin Cox estimate identified subgroup theta-hat*(H-hat): Bootstrap bias-corrected estimate Includes Cox-based HR AHR (Average Hazard Ratio loghr_po) estimators AHR columns present results. subgroup (H Hc) function reports: Avg: Mean estimates across estimable simulations. SD: Empirical standard deviation. Min / Max: Range. b-dagger: Relative bias (percent) vs marginal truth, 100 * (Avg - theta_dagger) / theta_dagger. b-ddagger (conditional): Relative bias (percent) vs CDE truth, shown CDE values available. bootstrap-corrected columns (hr.H.bc, hr.Hc.bc) present results, additional bias-corrected row (theta-hat*(H-hat)) added per subgroup. AHR columns (ahr.H.hat, ahr.Hc.hat) present, AHR estimation rows appended using DGM's true AHR values relative bias calculation. CDE columns (cde.H.hat, cde.Hc.hat) present CDE truth values available, CDE estimation rows (theta-ddagger(H-hat)) appended.  b-dagger column CDE rows reports bias relative CDE truth rather marginal HR.

title: Compute Detection Probability for GLM Outcomes — compute_detection_probability_glm
text: detection criterion (Leon et al., 2024, Section 2.1): Screening: \(W_1 + W_2 \ge 2k_1\) Consistency: \(\min(W_1, W_2) \ge k_2\) \(W_1, W_2 \sim N(\beta, 8/d_{\text{eff}})\) independently. ratio-scale effects, \(\beta = \log(\theta)\), \(k_j = \log(c_j)\). difference-scale effects, \(\beta = \theta\), \(k_j = c_j\).

title: Compute Naive and Split-Derived 95% CIs for Pareto Frontier Members — compute_frontier_cis
text: Naive CI: full-sample Wald CI Cox GLM model refit subgroup's data.  textbook CI ignores multiple-testing / subgroup-search context.  Anti-conservative construction. Split CI: 95\ estimate, SE estimated empirical standard deviation \(2S\) individual half-sample effect estimates produced n_splits random 50/50 splits.  half-jackknife SE (Shao1996).  Naming: \(\sim\) column labels marks resampling-derived approximation, model-based CI. FSBC-mimic CI: bias-corrected interval inspired bootstrap bias-correction algorithm Leon2024fs (eq 7), selection--bootstrap-data term \(\eta_b^*(\hat H_b^*)\) zeroed (selected subgroup treated fixed across half-jackknife replicates).  bias-corrected estimate \(\hat\beta^{\mathrm{FSBC}} = 2\hat\beta - \overline{\hat\beta^{(h)}}\) \(\overline{\hat\beta^{(h)}}\) mean \(2S\) half-sample estimates; SE half-jackknife SE Split CI.  See “Details — FSBC-mimic interpretation” . three CIs computed post-hoc returned forestsearch object; function modify internal state.

title: Compute Naive and Split-Derived 95% CIs for Pareto Frontier Members — compute_frontier_cis
text: n_splits random 50/50 splits fit effect model separately half, obtaining \(2S\) per-half estimates \(\{\hat\beta^{(s,h)} : s=1,\ldots,S; h=1,2\}\).  half-jackknife SE estimator $$\widehat{\mathrm{SE}} = \mathrm{sd}\bigl\{\hat\beta^{(s,h)}\bigr\},$$ .e., plain empirical SD \(2S\) estimates.  \(\sqrt{2}\) correction applied: simulation studies confirm estimator's CI achieves nominal coverage -selection setting (see package's pressure-test script).  Earlier versions function used average \((\hat\beta^{(s,1)} + \hat\beta^{(s,2)})/2\) per split; approach invalid two halves complementary average nearly constant.

title: Compute Naive and Split-Derived 95% CIs for Pareto Frontier Members — compute_frontier_cis
text: FSBC-mimic CI quick approximation bootstrap bias-corrected estimator Leon2024fs.  Substituting \(2S\) per-half estimates bootstrap replicates, treating selected subgroup \(\hat H\) fixed (.e., omitting \(\eta_b^*(\hat H_b^*) = \hat\beta_b^*(\hat H_b^*) - \hat\beta(\hat H_b^*)\) term captures variability FS selection bootstrap data), bias-corrected estimator paper eq (7) collapses $$\hat\beta^{\mathrm{FSBC}}(\hat H) = \hat\beta(\hat H) - \frac{1}{2S}\sum_{s,h}\bigl[\hat\beta^{(s,h)} - \hat\beta(\hat H)\bigr] = 2\hat\beta(\hat H) - \overline{\hat\beta^{(h)}}.$$ SE half-jackknife SE Split CI. FSBC-mimic CI full FSBC CI: omits selection--bootstrap-data variance.  Use column quick bias-corrected diagnostic, inference.  full FSBC CIs use forestsearch_bootstrap_dofuture.

what: Estimate heterogeneous treatment effects via DINA — dina_fit
title: Estimate heterogeneous treatment effects via DINA — dina_fit
text: dina_fit() implements two-step DINA (DIfference NAtural parameters) estimator Gao Hastie (2025) heterogeneous treatment effects (HTE) general response types: Gaussian (mean difference), binomial (log odds ratio), Poisson (log mean ratio), Cox (log hazard ratio). treatment effect assumed linear covariates, $$\tau(x) = \beta_0 + x^\top \beta_{1:d},$$ following Proposition 1 paper.  procedure two steps: (1) estimate nuisance functions \((x)\) \(\nu(x)\) training fold, (2) plug estimators GLM (Cox) likelihood held-fold estimate \(\beta\).  Cross-fitting averages two estimators obtained swapping folds.

text: Gaussian family uses simplification Section 3.2: \((x) = e(x)\) \(\nu(x) = E[Y \mid X = x]\), conditional outcome means \(\eta_0(x)\), \(\eta_1(x)\) required separately.  binomial Poisson families, separate within-arm fits \(\eta_0(x)\) \(\eta_1(x)\) used construct \((x)\) via modified propensity Eq. (12) paper.  Cox family, \((x)\) uses -censoring probabilities Eq. (18); estimated controlled cens_type. Variance estimation follows standard sandwich form: \(\widehat{V}(\hat\beta) = \widehat\Sigma_1^{-1} \widehat\Sigma_2 \widehat\Sigma_1^{-1} / n\), \(\widehat\Sigma_1\) \(\widehat\Sigma_2\) bread (negative score derivative) meat (outer product scores) matrices.  cross-fitting averaged across folds sandwich formed. what: forestsearch: Exploratory Subgroup Identification in Survival and GLM Outcomes — forestsearch-package
title: forestsearch: Exploratory Subgroup Identification in Survival and GLM Outcomes — forestsearch-package
text: Implements statistical methods exploratory subgroup identification clinical trials. Provides tools identifying patient subgroups differential treatment effects using machine learning approaches including Generalized Random Forests (GRF), LASSO regularization, exhaustive combinatorial search algorithms. Supports survival endpoints (Cox proportional hazards), binary outcomes (log odds ratio, log relative risk, risk difference), continuous outcomes (mean difference), count / rate outcomes (log incidence rate ratio via Poisson, quasi-Poisson, negative-binomial GLMs optional person-time offset). Features bootstrap bias correction using infinitesimal jackknife methods address selection bias post-hoc analyses. Designed clinical researchers conducting exploratory subgroup analyses randomized controlled trials, particularly multi-regional clinical trials (MRCT) requiring regional consistency evaluation. Methods described Leon et al. (2024) doi:10.1002/sim.10163 . Post-selection inference identified subgroup follows León Anderson (2026) doi:10.48550/arXiv.2609.38361 . search methodology given León Anderson (2026) doi:10.48550/arXiv.2610.28379 .

code: if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{ ## Example 1 -- Survival (GBSG, hormone therapy): the analysis of ## León and Anderson (2026a, Sec. 6) and of the survival-post-selection ## article on the package website. Forest search over the cut grid (no ## model-based front ends), effMaxSG selection in a 10% effect ## neighbourhood, multiplier-resampling inference for the reported ## subgroup computed inside the fit. library(survival) df_gbsg <- within(gbsg, {   id          <- seq_len(nrow(gbsg))   time_months <- rfstime / 30.4375   grade3      <- ifelse(grade == "3", 1, 0) }) fs_surv <- forestsearch(   df.analysis            = df_gbsg,   outcome.name           = "time_months",   event.name             = "status",   treat.name             = "hormon",   id.name                = "id",   confounders.name       = c("age", "meno", "size", "grade3", "nodes",                              "pgr", "er"),   is.RCT                 = TRUE,   use_lasso = FALSE, use_grf = FALSE, use_dina = FALSE,   conf.cont_jcuts        = list(er = 10, pgr = 10),   conf_force             = c("er <= 0", "pgr <= 0"),   subgroup_method        = "consistency",   sg_focus               = "effMaxSG",   selection_rule         = "neighborhood",   effect_neighborhood    = 0.10,   hr.threshold           = 1.0,   hr.consistency         = 1.0,   pconsistency.threshold = 0.90,   consistency_method     = "resample",   fs.splits              = 1000,   n.min = 60, d0.min = 10, d1.min = 10, maxk = 2,   mr_inference           = TRUE,   mr_inference_args      = list(draws = 5000L),   parallel_args          = list(plan = "multisession", workers = 4),   seedit                 = 8316951 ) print(fs_surv)  ## mr_estimates_table() lays the multiplier-resampling estimates out in the ## format of the bootstrap tables, so it takes a bootstrap result as its ## template (a few replicates are enough for the layout; the ## survival-post-selection article compares the two at full size). fs_boot <- forestsearch_bootstrap_dofuture(   fs.est        = fs_surv,   nb_boots      = 20,   parallel_args = list(plan = "multisession", workers = 4) ) mr_estimates_table(fs_surv, boot_results = fs_boot, est.scale = "hr")  ## Example 2 -- Binary outcome, odds ratio (ACTG175, ZDV+ddI vs ddI): ## the forest-search analysis of León and Anderson (2026a, Table S3); the ## binary analysis of León and Anderson (2026b) selects the same region ## with effect_neighborhood = 0.20. Adverse-scale outcome (1 = no CD4 ## improvement at week 20), OR thresholds at the null, same selection rule ## and multiplier-resampling gate as Example 1. if (requireNamespace("speff2trial", quietly = TRUE)) {   actg <- subset(speff2trial::ACTG175, arms %in% c(1L, 3L))   actg <- actg[!is.na(actg$cd420), ]   actg$id           <- seq_len(nrow(actg))   actg$treat        <- as.integer(actg$arms == 1L)   actg$y_binary_neg <- as.integer(!(actg$cd420 > actg$cd40))   bin_vars <- c("hemo", "homo", "drugs", "race", "gender", "symptom")   for (v in bin_vars) actg[[v]] <- as.numeric(actg[[v]])   fs_bin <- forestsearch(     df.analysis            = actg,     outcome.name           = "y_binary_neg",     event.name             = "y_binary_neg",     treat.name             = "treat",     id.name                = "id",     confounders.name       = c("age", "preanti", "wtkg", "karnof", "cd40",                                "cd80", bin_vars),     outcome_type           = "binary",     effect_measure         = "OR",     adverse_outcome        = TRUE,     use_lasso = FALSE, use_grf = FALSE, use_dina = FALSE,     conf.cont_jcuts        = list(cd40 = 10, wtkg = 10),     subgroup_method        = "consistency",     sg_focus               = "effMaxSG",     selection_rule         = "neighborhood",     effect_neighborhood    = 0.10,     effect.threshold       = 1.0,     consistency.threshold  = 1.0,     pconsistency.threshold = 0.90,     consistency_method     = "resample",     fs.splits              = 500,     n.min = 60, d0.min = 10, d1.min = 10, maxk = 2,     mr_inference           = TRUE,     mr_inference_args      = list(draws = 5000L),     parallel_args          = list(plan = "multisession", workers = 4),     seedit                 = 8316951   )   print(fs_bin) }  ## Example 3 -- Continuous outcome, mean difference (ACTG175): the ## continuous application of León and Anderson (2026b), with the field ## (calibrated one-sided) bounds for the selected subgroup and its ## complement. Outcome is CD4 decline from baseline to week 20 (adverse ## scale); thresholds are on the mean-difference scale. if (requireNamespace("speff2trial", quietly = TRUE)) {   actg <- subset(speff2trial::ACTG175, arms %in% c(1L, 3L))   actg <- actg[!is.na(actg$cd420), ]   actg$id        <- seq_len(nrow(actg))   actg$treat     <- as.integer(actg$arms == 1L)   actg$y_decline <- actg$cd40 - actg$cd420   bin_vars <- c("hemo", "homo", "drugs", "race", "gender", "symptom")   for (v in bin_vars) actg[[v]] <- as.factor(actg[[v]])   fs_cont <- forestsearch(     df.analysis            = actg,     outcome.name           = "y_decline",     treat.name             = "treat",     id.name                = "id",     confounders.name       = c("age", "preanti", "wtkg", "karnof", "cd40",                                "cd80", bin_vars),     outcome_type           = "continuous",     effect_measure         = "MD",     adverse_outcome        = TRUE,     use_lasso = FALSE, use_grf = FALSE, use_dina = FALSE,     conf.cont_jcuts        = list(age = 10, preanti = 10, wtkg = 10,                                   karnof = 10, cd40 = 10, cd80 = 10),     sg_focus               = "effMaxSG",     selection_rule         = "neighborhood",     effect_neighborhood    = 0.20,     effect.threshold       = 10,     consistency.threshold  = 5,     pconsistency.threshold = 0.90,     consistency_method     = "resample",     fs.splits              = 500,     n.min = 60, d0.min = 10, d1.min = 10, maxk = 2,     mr_inference           = TRUE,     mr_inference_args      = list(ci_method = "field", draws = 5000L,                                   include_complement = TRUE,                                   field_complement = TRUE,                                   field_scale_complement = "selected",                                   return_reselection = TRUE),     parallel_args          = list(plan = "sequential"),     seedit                 = 8316951   )   print(fs_cont) } } # }

text: Two bias correction approaches implemented: Method 1 (Simple Optimism): $$H_{adj1} = H_{obs} - (H^*_{*} - H^*_{obs})$$ \(H^*_{*}\) new subgroup HR bootstrap data \(H^*_{obs}\) new subgroup HR original data.
