code: set.seed(11) n <- 200 df <- data.frame(id = seq_len(n), treat = rbinom(n, 1, 0.5),                  age = round(rnorm(n, 55, 12)),                  bm = factor(rbinom(n, 1, 0.5))) harm <- df$age <= 50 & df$bm == "1" tt <- rexp(n, 0.05 * exp(log(2.5) * df$treat * harm)) df$time <- pmin(tt, 60) df$event <- as.integer(tt <= 60) fit <- forestsearch(   df.analysis = df,   outcome.name = "time", event.name = "event",   treat.name = "treat", id.name = "id",   confounders.name = c("age", "bm"),   sg_focus = "maxeff", use_grf = FALSE, use_lasso = FALSE,   fs.splits = 50, n.min = 30, d0.min = 5, d1.min = 5,   hr.threshold = 1.1, hr.consistency = 1.0,   pconsistency.threshold = 0.5, maxk = 2,   details = FALSE, plot.sg = FALSE,   parallel_args = list(plan = "sequential", workers = 1L,                        show_message = FALSE) ) #> Warning: sg_focus = 'maxeff' selects the effect maximiser with no auxiliary conditions; overriding: pconsistency.threshold -> 0, stop_threshold -> NULL, use_twostage -> FALSE, minp -> 0. The subgroup-search effect floor (hr.threshold) is disabled, redundancy pruning is relaxed to exact-duplicate removal (rmin -> 0), and consistency-stage duplicate removal collapses identical-membership candidates to their fewest-cut representative -- so the argmax ranges over the full estimable family with no arbitrary tie-break. #>  #> [forestsearch] Subgroup Identification Configuration #>   Outcome type:   survival (Cox PH) #>   Effect measure: HR (hazard ratio) #>   Scale:          log (ratio) #>  #>   Screening:      HR >= 1.10  (log: 0.0953) #>   Consistency:    HR >= 1.00  (log: 0.0000) #>   Consistency rate threshold: 0% #>  #>   Interpretation: #>     Candidates: subgroup hazard ratio >= 1.10 #>     Splits:     each split HR >= 1.00 gh <- fs_to_guohe(fit, time = "time", event = "event",                   treatment = "treat", B = 50, seed = 3) gh$naive_hr #> [1] 1.285522 gh$debiased_hr #> [1] 0.8041826 gh$bound_hr #> [1] 0.5205394

text: data data frame containing source dataset. factor_vars Character vector factor/categorical variable names include covariates. candidate confounders ForestSearch (e.g., paste0("z", 1:12)). continuous_vars Character vector continuous variable names include prognostic covariates baseline GLM.  improve model fit participate subgroup definition. Consistent generate_aft_dgm_flex, accepts continuous_vars factor_vars.  Default NULL (factor-model, backward compatible). outcome_var Character string naming outcome variable. treatment_var Character string naming treatment variable (must 0/1 coded). outcome_type Character. One "binary", "continuous", "count". effect_measure Character. Effect measure GLM. Default NULL, selects "" binary, "MD" continuous, "IRR" count outcomes. offset_var Character NULL. Name exposure / follow-time column count outcomes offset. Required effect_measure "IRR" "IRD".  offset enters Poisson GLM offset(log(offset_var)).  Default NULL. subgroup_vars Character vector variable names defining subgroup. Default NULL (subgroup). subgroup_cuts Named list cutpoint specifications subgroup variables. Uses flexible format generate_aft_dgm_flex: fixed values, quantiles, functions. model Character. "alt" alternative hypothesis treatment–subgroup interaction, "null" uniform treatment effect. Default "alt". k_treat Numeric. Scaling factor fitted treatment coefficient linear predictor scale.  k_treat = 1 (default) preserves fitted treatment effect -. k_treat > 1 amplifies treatment main effect, useful source dataset weak treatment effect stronger ITT desired simulation.  k_treat < 1 attenuates effect.  Analogous k_treat parameter generate_aft_dgm_flex. Note: null DGM (model = "null") represents homogeneous treatment effect (HTE), zero treatment effect.  k_treat scales magnitude homogeneous effect. k_inter Numeric. Direct additive shift linear predictor Q members treatment.  interpretation depends outcome_type: binary Shift log-odds scale. Positive increases P(Y=1) Q treatment. continuous Shift mean scale (identity link). Positive increases \(E(Y)\) Q treatment. count Shift log-rate scale. Positive increases \(E(Y)\) Q treatment (multiplicative: rate multiplied exp(k_inter)). Default 0 (interaction, equivalent model = "null"). adverse_outcome Logical.  TRUE outcome_type = "binary", interaction shift k_inter negated internally positive k_inter consistently amplifies treatment contrast beneficial (1 - Y) scale.  flag stored returned object downstream use calibrate_glm_interaction run_simulation_analysis.  Default FALSE. n_super Integer. Size super-population. Default 5000L. seed Integer. Random seed super-population sampling. Default 8316951L. verbose Logical. Print diagnostic information. Default FALSE. k_random_noise Integer. Number standard-normal noise columns (noise1, noise2, ...) drawn onto super-population construction. Default 0L (noise columns; output identical previous versions). noise_seed Integer. Seed population-level noise draw, used k_random_noise > 0. Default 20260807L, committed population-noise seed (commit 2a4787bc).

text: df.analysis Data frame containing data. use_lasso Logical. Whether use LASSO dimension reduction. use_grf Logical. Whether use GRF cuts. grf_cuts Character vector GRF cut expressions. confounders.name Character vector confounder variable names. cont.cutoff Integer. Cutoff continuous variable determination. conf_force Character vector forced cut expressions. conf.cont_medians Character vector continuous confounders cut median. conf.cont_medians_force Character vector additional continuous confounders force median cut. conf.cont_jcuts Named list positive integers, one per continuous confounder J-quantile cuts desired.  variable X listed X = J, default cut set (cut_var(): mean, median, Q1, Q3) replaced J binary cut points (k/(J+1))-th quantiles X k = 1, ..., J, defining J+1 non-overlapping intervals $$[\min(X), c_1),\ [c_1, c_2),\ \ldots,\ [c_J, \max(X)].$$ Variables listed retain default behaviour.  J-quantile cuts unconditional (filtered LASSO), matching defaultcut_names semantics.  Names must confounders.name must overlap defaultcut_names conf.cont_medians_force. dina_cuts Character vector DINA cut expressions (optional), merged candidate pool exactly like grf_cuts. collapse_cuts Logical.  TRUE, collapse near-redundant continuous candidate cuts full pool assembled resolved literal numerics.  Cuts variable operator whose thresholds lie within per-variable standard-error band merged single rounded-centroid threshold, subject membership safety check; see collapse_redundant_cuts.  Categorical, indicator, bare-name equality cuts untouched.  Default TRUE; pass collapse_cuts = FALSE recover un-coarsened candidate pool used earlier package versions. collapse_cuts_args List overrides coarsening, merged onto defaults list(c = 1.0, tol = 0.05, digits = 0L): c band multiplier (band = c * sd(x)/sqrt(n)), tol membership safety tolerance (fraction n < 1, absolute count >= 1), digits rounding representative threshold. Ignored collapse_cuts = FALSE. replace_med_grf Logical. TRUE, removes median cuts overlap GRF cuts. defaultcut_names Character vector confounders force default cuts. cut_type Character. "default" "median" cut strategy. exclude_cuts Character vector cut expressions exclude. outcome.name Character. Name outcome variable. event.name Character. Name event indicator variable. details Logical. TRUE, prints details execution. outcome_type Character. One "survival" (default), "binary", "continuous". offset.name Character NULL. Name follow-time column rate-based measures (IRR, IRD).

Name continuous biomarker covariate. Default: "bm". family Character family object.  One "binomial" (default), "poisson", "gaussian".  Determines link function scale treatment-effect profile: "binomial" uses logit link (profile log-); "poisson" uses log link (profile log-IRR, requires offset_name); "gaussian" uses identity link (profile mean difference). offset_name Character NULL.  Name offset variable (e.g., log follow-time Poisson models).  offset applied log(offset_var) internally.  Required family = "poisson". alpha Numeric. Significance level confidence intervals (two-sided).  Default: 0.05 (95 percent CI). spline_df Integer. Degrees freedom natural spline. Default: 3. z_by Numeric. Increment biomarker prediction grid. Point estimates log treatment effect (log-, log-IRR, MD) grid point. loghr_lower Numeric vector. Lower confidence bounds. loghr_upper Numeric vector. Upper confidence bounds. se_loghr Numeric vector. Standard errors (delta method). counts_profile Integer vector. Observation counts near grid point. glm_primary Numeric. Overall treatment effect -interaction GLM. model_fit fitted glm object. spline_basis natural spline basis object. family Character. GLM family used. effect_label Character. Human-readable label effect scale (e.g., "log()", "log(IRR)", "Mean Difference"). lrt_pvalue Numeric. P-value likelihood ratio test comparing interaction model main-effects-model. alpha Numeric. Significance level used. ci_level Numeric. Confidence level (1 - alpha). Invisibly returns x.

title: Fit GLM with Spline Treatment-Biomarker Interaction — glm_cs_fit
text: binary outcomes (family = "binomial"): $$\text{logit}(P(Y=1|Z,)) = \beta_0 + f(Z) + g(Z) \cdot $$ count outcomes offset (family = "poisson"): $$\log(E[Y|Z,]) = \beta_0 + f(Z) + g(Z) \cdot + \log(t)$$ continuous outcomes (family = "gaussian"): $$E[Y|Z,] = \beta_0 + f(Z) + g(Z) \cdot $$ treatment-effect profile \(\beta(Z) = \beta_0 + g(Z)\) estimated link scale (log-, log-IRR, identity) pointwise delta-method confidence intervals.

title: Plot Subgroup Results Forest Plot — plot_subgroup_results_forestplot
text: fs_results List. list containing ForestSearch analysis results elements: fs.est: ForestSearch estimation object forestsearch fs_bc: Bootstrap bias-corrected results forestsearch_bootstrap_dofuture fs_kfold: K-fold cross-validation results forestsearch_Kfold forestsearch_tenfold (optional) fs_OOB: --bag cross-validation results (optional, alternative fs_kfold) df_analysis Data frame. analysis dataset outcome, event, treatment variables. subgroup_list List. Named list subgroup definitions include plot. element list : subset_expr: Character string subsetting (e.g., "BM> 1") name: Display name subgroup type: Either "reference" pre-specified "posthoc" identified outcome.name Character. Name survival time variable. event.name Character. Name event indicator variable. treat.name Character. Name treatment variable. E.name Character. Label experimental arm (default: "Experimental"). C.name Character. Label control arm (default: "Control"). est.scale Character. Estimate scale: "hr" "1/hr" (default: "hr"). xlog Logical. TRUE (default), x-axis plotted logarithmic scale. standard hazard ratio forest plots equal distances represent equal relative effects. Implemented forestploter's set_xaxis(x_trans = "log") since 0.4.0.9000; earlier versions documented log axis drew linear one (GitHub #7). title_text Character. Plot title (default: NULL). arrow_text Character vector length 2. Arrow labels forest plot (default: c("Favors Experimental", "Favors Control")). footnote_text Character vector. Footnote text plot explaining CV metrics (default provides CV interpretation guidance; set NULL omit). xlim Numeric vector length 2. X-axis limits (default: c(0.25, 1.5)). ticks_at Numeric vector. X-axis tick positions (default: c(0.25, 0.70, 1.0, 1.5)). show_cv_metrics Logical. Whether show cross-validation metrics (default: TRUE fs_kfold fs_OOB available). cv_source Character. Source CV metrics: "auto" (default, uses available, otherwise whichever present), "kfold" (use fs_kfold ), "oob" (use fs_OOB ), "" (explicitly use fs_kfold fs_OOB, K-fold first OOB). posthoc_colors Character vector. Colors post-hoc subgroup rows (default: c("powderblue", "beige")). reference_colors Character vector. Colors reference subgroup rows (default: c("yellow", "powderblue")). ci_column_spaces Integer. Number spaces CI plot column width. spaces = wider CI column (default: 20). conf.level Numeric. Confidence level intervals (default: 0.95 95% CI). Used calculate z-multiplier qnorm(1 - (1 - conf.level)/2). theme fs_forest_theme object create_forest_theme(). Use control plot sizing (fonts, row height, CI appearance, CV annotation font size). Default: NULL (uses default theme). outcome_type Character NULL. One "survival" (default), "binary", "continuous".  NULL, auto-detected fs_results$fs.est$outcome_type. effect_measure Character NULL. Effect measure GLM outcomes (e.g., "", "RR", "IRR", "RD", "IRD", "MD").  Auto-detected fs_results$fs.est$effect_measure NULL. offset.name Character NULL. Follow-time column rate-based measures (IRR, IRD). adjust_covariates option implemented tested manuscript analyses simulation studies León Anderson (2026a, 2026b), use unadjusted treatment-fits. Character vector NULL. Baseline covariates adjust GLM-row effect models , matching adjustment used search/estimation.  NULL, resolved fs_results$fs.est$args_call_all$adjust_covariates forest-plot CIs share fit's scale.  Applies GLM rows . extreme_ci_cap Numeric. Multiplier outlier-resistant axis limits xlim_method = "data".  extreme CI bound exceeds twice second-extreme, axis limit capped extreme_ci_cap times second-extreme bound. Default 1.5.  Set Inf disable. xlim_method Character. Method computing default axis limits GLM measures xlim user-supplied. "clinical" (default) uses fixed clinically meaningful ranges: HR//RR/IRR = (0.25, 4.0), RD/IRD = (-0.50, 0.50), MD = data-driven. "data" computes limits actual estimates outlier resistance controlled extreme_ci_cap.

title: Prepare Censoring Model Parameters — prepare_censoring_model
text: df_work Working data frame (output prepare_working_dataset). cens_type Character. "weibull" "uniform". cens_params Named list user-supplied censoring parameters. df_super Super-population data frame; receives lin_pred_cens_0 lin_pred_cens_1 columns. select_censoring Logical. Selects among three censoring modes: AIC selection select_censoring = TRUE (default): fits censoring distribution observed data via AIC comparison among four survreg candidates – Weibull LogNormal, covariates intercept-. Analytical select_censoring = FALSE cens_params supplies required analytical parameters (mu+tau Weibull/LogNormal; min+max uniform optional defaulting): fitting; uses cens_params directly; covariate contribution zero. Force-fit select_censoring = FALSE cens_params supply analytical parameters (Weibull/LogNormal ): fits chosen distribution formula determined cens_intercept_only censoring covariate vectors – AIC arbitration, fallback intercept-. cens_intercept_only Logical. honored force-fit mode (select_censoring = FALSE empty cens_params). TRUE, fits Surv(y, 1 - event) ~ 1 (treat, covariates).  FALSE (default), formula determined censoring covariate vectors: *_cens = NULL (default): inherit outcome model; formula ~ treat + zcens_<outcome covariates>. *_cens = character(0): treat-; formula ~ treat. One *_cens non-empty: formula ~ treat + zcens_<supplied covariates>. Setting cens_intercept_only = TRUE select_censoring = TRUE analytical cens_params raises error. verbose Logical. TRUE (default), prints censoring model comparison table recommendation. Set FALSE suppress censoring model selection output.

title: Prepare Censoring Model Parameters — prepare_censoring_model
text: named list: cens_model List censoring distribution parameters stored dgm$model_params$censoring. df_super Updated super-population data frame lin_pred_cens_0 lin_pred_cens_1 appended.  hold covariate contributions (\(\gamma_c' X\)); intercept excluded.

title: Prepare Censoring Model Parameters — prepare_censoring_model
text: lin_pred_cens_0 lin_pred_cens_1 store covariate contribution — .e. \(\gamma_c' X\), intercept \(\mu_c\) excluded.  matches convention used outcome model (lin_pred_0, lin_pred_1 = \(\gamma' X\), intercept) computed calculate_linear_predictors(). simulate_from_dgm() reconstructs full log-censoring time : $$\log C = \mu_c + \delta + \tau_c \epsilon + \gamma_c' X$$ \(\mu_c\) = params$censoring$mu, \(\delta\) = cens_adjust, \(\tau_c\) = params$censoring$tau, \(\gamma_c' X\) = lin_pred_cens_{0|1}. select_censoring = TRUE, predict(survreg, type = "linear") returns full linear predictor \(\mu_c + \gamma_c' X\).  stored intercept \(\mu_c\) therefore subtracted writing lin_pred_cens_*, simulate_from_dgm() can add params$censoring$mu exactly .  Omitting subtraction causes \(\mu_c\) counted twice, producing astronomically large censoring times universal censoring. select_censoring = FALSE Weibull/lognormal cens_type, intercept-model zero covariate contribution, lin_pred_cens_0 = lin_pred_cens_1 = 0.  Storing mu instead 0 causes double-counting.

title: Reset a Parallel Worker Pool — reset_workers
text: workers Integer.  Number workers new pool. Default NULL leaves current plan's worker count unchanged (useful reset without resize wanted; requires future installed). strategy Character.  future strategy reinstate.  Default "multisession".  reasonable choices "multicore" (Linux/macOS ) "sequential" (disable parallelism entirely). sleep Numeric.  Seconds pause teardown setup.  Default 1.  Set 0 skip. gc Logical.  Whether force garbage collection teardown setup.  Default TRUE. quiet Logical.  Suppress informational message() output.  Default FALSE.

title: Reset a Parallel Worker Pool — reset_workers
text: Invisibly, list previous current plan class names: list(previous = <chr>, current = <chr>).

title: Reset a Parallel Worker Pool — reset_workers
text: worker reset sequence : future::plan("sequential") – dismantles existing worker pool; R processes terminate memory returned OS. gc(verbose = FALSE) – reclaims main-process memory holding references now-defunct futures. Sys.sleep(sleep) – brief pause let OS reclaim sockets / pipes new pool requested. small non-zero sleep (default 1) materially reduces multisession setup failures observed busy Linux servers; set 0 skip. future::plan(strategy, workers = workers) – starts fresh pool. function -op future installed requested strategy initialised; warning emitted previous plan left place.

title: Reset a Parallel Worker Pool — reset_workers

title: Run Null Calibration Simulation — run_null_calibration
code: # \donttest{ # Binary DGM under H0 sim_null <- function(n, seed) {   set.seed(seed)   data.frame(     id = seq_len(n),     treat = rbinom(n, 1, 0.5),     bm1 = as.factor(rbinom(n, 1, 0.70)),     bm2 = as.factor(rbinom(n, 1, 0.50)),     age = round(rnorm(n, 55, 10)),     ecog = as.factor(sample(0:1, n, TRUE, c(0.6, 0.4))),     progressed = rbinom(n, 1, 0.30)   ) }  fs_args <- list(   confounders.name = c("bm1", "bm2", "age", "ecog"),   outcome.name = "progressed",   event.name = "progressed",   treat.name = "treat",   id.name = "id",   outcome_type = "binary",   effect_measure = "OR",   adverse_outcome = TRUE,   pconsistency.threshold = 0.90,   fs.splits = 200,   n.min = 60,   maxk = 2,   use_lasso = FALSE,   use_grf = FALSE,   use_twostage = TRUE,   is.RCT = TRUE,   details = FALSE,   plot.sg = FALSE,   parallel_args = list(plan = "sequential",                        workers = 1,                        show_message = FALSE) )  # Illustrative size only (the function requires n_sims >= 10 and at least # two N values); a calibration for use takes n_sims of 50 or more over the # trial sizes of interest. cal <- run_null_calibration(   sim_null_fn = sim_null,   fs_args = fs_args,   d_eff_fn = function(n) d_eff_binary(n, 0.30),   N_values = c(200, 500),   n_sims = 10,   verbose = TRUE ) #> Null calibration: 2 N values x 10 sims = 20 tasks #>   N =  200: FPR = 0.200 (2/10) | P1 = 0.227 | 1.3 sec #>   N =  500: FPR = 0.500 (5/10) | P1 = 0.195 | 2.2 sec #>  #> L_eff Calibration #>   Model: L_eff = 0.157 * (N / 60)^1.421 #>   R-squared: 1.000 #>   Calibrated at N = 200, 500 #>  #>   Implied L_eff: #>     N =  200: L_eff = 0.87 (fitted: 0.87) #>     N =  500: L_eff = 3.19 (fitted: 3.19) print(cal) #> L_eff Calibration #>   Model: L_eff = 0.157 * (N / 60)^1.421 #>   R-squared: 1.000 #>   Calibrated at N = 200, 500 #>  #>   Implied L_eff: #>     N =  200: L_eff = 0.87 (fitted: 0.87) #>     N =  500: L_eff = 3.19 (fitted: 3.19) # }

Two forms accepted: character vector canonical "<engine>-<focus>" labels, e.g. c("fs-effMaxSG", "dina-effMaxSG", "grf-tree"), expanded internally per-arm forestsearch() overrides.  Engines "fs" (subgroup_method = "consistency"), "dina", "grf" (grf_selection = "frontier", "tree" grf-tree label).  Defaults applied expansion: selection_rule = "neighborhood"; fs-* arms use_grf = TRUE, use_dina = TRUE, use_lasso = FALSE, n.min = NULL (sample-size-adaptive rule). named list explicit forestsearch() argument-override lists, label = name, e.g. list("fs-effMaxSG" = list(subgroup_method = "consistency", sg_focus = "effMaxSG", use_grf = TRUE, use_dina = TRUE, use_lasso = FALSE), "grf-tree" = list(subgroup_method = "grf", grf_selection = "tree")). arm's overrides merged top default_sim_params() overlaid fs_params; per-arm overrides take precedence.  merge preserves explicit n.min = NULL.  Default NULL preserves legacy boolean behavior. fs_params Named list ForestSearch parameter overrides.  element default_sim_params() can overridden, including parallel_args (see Parallel Processing section ). Passing NULL empty list uses defaults throughout. grf_params Named list GRF parameter overrides. cox_formula Optional Cox formula unadjusted ITT. cox_formula_adj Optional adjusted Cox formula. n_sims_total Integer. Total simulations (progress messages). seed_base Integer. Base seed; replicate seed = seed_base + sim_id. Default 8316951L. verbose Logical. Print progress messages. Default FALSE. verbose_n Integer. set, print sim_id <= verbose_n. Default NULL. debug Logical. Print detailed debug output. Default FALSE. keep Character vector. Optional names heavy diagnostic objects attach list attr(result, "diagnostics"). Allowed values (combination): "fs_full" full forestsearch() result object (minus df.est analysis data frame, stripped control memory).  Includes sg.harm, grp.consistency, confounders.candidate, confounders.evaluated, GRF cuts, timing. "df.est" analysis data frame treat.recommend column attached.  Heavy; use sparingly. "candidate_table" data table candidate subgroups evaluated (fs_full$grp.consistency$out_sg$result).  Medium-weight; useful diagnosing candidates near-threshold. "grf_full" full grf.subg.harm.*() result object. Default character(0) (attach nothing; current behavior). keep_first_n Integer.  keep non-empty, attach requested diagnostics sim_id <= keep_first_n. title: Sort Subgroups by Focus (post-consistency) — sort_subgroups
text: Sorts data.table subgroup results according specified focus. "hrMaxSG" "hrMinSG", candidates first partitioned candidate inclusion set ("band"), ranked within band sample size.  selection_rule argument controls band defined: "neighborhood" – 1D effect-size band (default; legacy behaviour): candidate -band iff effect within effect_neighborhood maximum. title: Sort Subgroups by Focus (post-consistency) — sort_subgroups
text: result_new data.table subgroup results columns Pcons, hr, N, K. sg_focus Character. Sorting focus.  One "hr", "maxSG", "hrMaxSG", "minSG", "hrMinSG". selection_rule Character. Rule defining candidate inclusion set "hrMaxSG" / "hrMinSG".  One "neighborhood" (default; current behaviour), "pareto", "".  Must "neighborhood" sg_focus values. effect_neighborhood Numeric [0, 1).  Relative tolerance defining effect-size neighborhood "hrMaxSG" "hrMinSG".  candidate neighborhood iff (natural-scale) effect least (1 - effect_neighborhood) * max(effect).  Default 0.10 (.e., within 10\ selection_rule "neighborhood" ""; ignored "pareto" (rejected non-default "pareto"). effect_log_scale Logical.  TRUE, hr column stores log-scale values (log-, log-IRR) exponentiated applying inclusion test.  Default FALSE (Cox stores natural-scale HR).

title: Sort Subgroups by Focus (post-consistency) — sort_subgroups
text: sorted data.table.  top row selected subgroup sg_focus; remaining rows diagnostic.

title: Sort Subgroups by Focus (post-consistency) — sort_subgroups
text: Sort keys sg_focus: "hr" (-Pcons, -hr, K) – prefer high consistency large effect. "maxSG" (-N, -Pcons, K) – prefer large subgroups high consistency. "minSG" (N, -Pcons, K) – prefer small subgroups high consistency. "hrMaxSG" (-in_band, -N, -Pcons, -hr, K) – among candidates inclusion band defined selection_rule, prefer largest sample size. "hrMinSG" (-in_band, N, -Pcons, -hr, K) – among candidates inclusion band defined selection_rule, prefer smallest sample size. "hrMaxSG" "hrMinSG" use lexicographic candidate band rule: effect size primary, bounded set candidates near (trading ) maximum accepted optimize sample size. Selection rules: "neighborhood" 1D \(\varepsilon\)-band effect scale: in_band = (hr >= (1 - effect_neighborhood) * max(hr)). Setting effect_neighborhood = 0 reduces strict max-effect filter.  legacy behaviour. "pareto" 2D Pareto-non-dominated set: candidate -band iff candidate hr_j >= hr_i N_j >= N_i least one strict inequality.  Reuses dominance computation compute_pareto_frontier(). Removes effect_neighborhood tuning parameter selection criterion. "" Intersection: -band iff \(\varepsilon\)-band Pareto-non-dominated.  Strictest three.
